translations.literal: Volume 107.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 107.

sentences.zh: 【晉紀二十九】 起強圉大淵獻，盡重光單閼，凡五年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 29] From Qiangyu Dayuanxian through Chongguang Danyan; five years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 29] From Qiangyu Dayuanxian through Chongguang Danyan—five years in all.

sentences.zh: 列宗孝武皇帝中之下太元十二年（

translations.literal: Middle and lower portion of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the twelfth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: From the middle and latter part of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the twelfth year of the Taiyuan era (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元三八七年）

translations.literal: dinghai, corresponding to the year 387 CE).
translations.idiomatic: dinghai, corresponding to 387 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙巳，以朱序為青，兗二州刺史，代謝玄鎮彭城；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yisi, Zhu Xu was appointed Inspector of Qing and Yan Provinces, replacing Xie Xuan in garrisoning Pengcheng;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's yisi day, Zhu Xu was made Inspector of Qing and Yan, taking over Xie Xuan's post at Pengcheng;

sentences.zh: 序求鎮淮陰，許之。

translations.literal: Xu requested to be stationed at Huaiyin, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xu asked to command from Huaiyin, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 以玄為會稽內史。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan was appointed Administrator of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan was named Administrator of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingwei, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day the court declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂觀兵河上，高陽王隆曰：「溫詳之徒，皆白面儒生，烏合為群，徒恃長河以自固，若大軍濟河，必望旗震壞，不待戰也。」

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui reviewed his troops on the riverbank. The Prince of Gaoyang, Long, said, "Wen Xiang and his sort are all pale-faced scholars who have banded together in a mob; they rely only on the long river to hold themselves secure. If our great army crosses the river, they will surely crumble at the sight of our banners without waiting for battle."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, lord of Yan, reviewed his army on the river. Prince Murong Long of Gaoyang said, "Men like Wen Xiang are pale-faced literati cobbled into a crowd; they trust only the broad river for safety. Once our main force crosses, they will break at the sight of our standards—no battle needed."

sentences.zh: 垂從之。

translations.literal: Chui followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Chui agreed.

sentences.zh: 戊午，遣鎮北將軍蘭汗、護軍將軍平幼於碻磝西四十里濟河，隆以大眾陳於北岸。

translations.literal: On wuwu he sent the Pacifier of the North, Lan Han, and the Protector-General, Ping You, to cross the river forty li west of Que'ao, while Long arrayed a great host on the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he sent Lan Han, Pacifier of the North, and Ping You, Protector-General, to ford the river forty li west of Que'ao, while Long drew up the main army on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 溫攀、溫楷果走趣城，平幼追擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Wen Pan and Wen Kai indeed fled toward the city; Ping You pursued and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Pan and Wen Kai did flee for the city; Ping You chased them down and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 詳夜將妻子奔彭城，其眾三萬餘戶皆降於燕。

translations.literal: That night Xiang led his wife and children in flight to Pengcheng; more than thirty thousand households of his followers all surrendered to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang fled by night with his family to Pengcheng, and more than thirty thousand households of his followers surrendered to Yan.

sentences.zh: 垂以太原王楷為兗州刺史，鎮東阿。

translations.literal: Chui appointed the Prince of Taiyuan, Kai, Inspector of Yan Province and stationed him at Dong'e.
translations.idiomatic: Chui made Prince Murong Kai of Taiyuan Inspector of Yan and posted him at Dong'e.

sentences.zh: 初，垂在長安，秦王堅嘗與之交手語，垂出，冗從僕射光祚言於堅曰：「陛下頗疑慕容垂乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chui was at Chang'an, King Fu Jian of Qin had once spoken with him hand in hand; after Chui left, the attendant master of ceremonies Guang Zuo said to Jian, "Your Majesty, do you rather suspect Murong Chui?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Chui was at Chang'an, King Fu Jian of Former Qin had spoken with him familiarly, hand in hand. After Chui left, Attendant Master of Ceremonies Guang Zuo said to Jian, "Does Your Majesty harbor doubts about Murong Chui?

sentences.zh: 垂非久為人下者也。」

translations.literal: Chui is not one to remain long beneath another."
translations.idiomatic: He is not a man who will stay beneath others for long."

sentences.zh: 堅以告垂。

translations.literal: Jian told Chui of this.
translations.idiomatic: Jian repeated the remark to Chui.

sentences.zh: 及秦主丕自鄴奔晉陽，祚與黃門侍郎封孚、巨鹿太守封勸皆來奔。

translations.literal: When the Qin ruler Pi fled from Ye to Jinyang, Guang Zuo, Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gates Feng Fu, and the Administrator of Julu Feng Quan all came over to Chui's side.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin ruler Fu Pi fled Ye for Jinyang, Guang Zuo, Gentleman Attendant Feng Fu, and Julu Administrator Feng Quan all defected to Chui.

sentences.zh: 勸，弈之子也。

translations.literal: Quan was the son of Feng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was Feng Yi's son.

sentences.zh: 垂之再圍鄴也，秦故臣西河朱肅等各以其眾來奔。

translations.literal: When Chui besieged Ye a second time, former Qin ministers such as Zhu Su of Xihe each came over with their followers.
translations.idiomatic: During Chui's second siege of Ye, former Qin officials including Zhu Su of Xihe arrived with their troops.

sentences.zh: 詔以祚等為河北諸郡太守，皆營於濟北、濮陽，羈屬溫詳；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Guang Zuo and the others governors of various Hebei commanderies; all encamped at Jibei and Puyang and were placed under Wen Xiang's restraint;
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Guang Zuo and the others administrators of Hebei commanderies; they camped at Jibei and Puyang under Wen Xiang's oversight;

sentences.zh: 詳敗，俱詣燕軍降。

translations.literal: when Xiang was defeated, all went to the Yan army and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: when Xiang fell, they all went to the Yan camp and submitted.

sentences.zh: 垂赦之，撫待如舊。

translations.literal: Chui pardoned them and treated them as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chui pardoned them and received them as of old.

sentences.zh: 垂見光祚，流涕沾衿，曰：「秦主待我深，吾事之亦盡；

translations.literal: When Chui saw Guang Zuo, tears soaked his collar. He said, "The Qin ruler treated me with deep kindness, and I served him with full loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Guang Zuo, Chui wept until his collar was wet and said, "The Qin ruler was deeply kind to me, and I served him with all I had;

sentences.zh: 但為二公猜忌，吾懼死而負之，每一念之，中宵不寐。」

translations.literal: but because those two lords were suspicious of me, I feared death and failing him; whenever I think of it, I cannot sleep through the night."
translations.idiomatic: yet those two lords grew suspicious, and I feared I would die still owing him a debt—whenever I think of it, I lie awake till midnight."

sentences.zh: 祚亦悲慟。

translations.literal: Guang Zuo was also overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Zuo wept as well.

sentences.zh: 垂賜祚金帛，祚固辭，垂曰：「卿猶復疑邪？」

translations.literal: Chui bestowed gold and silk on Guang Zuo, but Guang Zuo firmly declined. Chui said, "Do you still harbor doubts?"
translations.idiomatic: Chui offered Guang Zuo gold and silk; Guang Zuo refused firmly. Chui said, "Do you still doubt me?"

sentences.zh: 詐曰：「臣昔者惟知忠於所事，不意陛下至今懷之，臣敢逃其死？」

translations.literal: Guang Zuo said, "Your servant once knew only loyalty to the master he served; I did not expect Your Majesty still to bear this against me—how dare I flee death?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang Zuo said, "I once knew only loyalty to my lord; I never thought Your Majesty would still hold it against me—how could I shirk death?"

sentences.zh: 祚曰：「此乃卿之忠，固吾求也，前言戲之耳」。

translations.literal: Chui said, "This is precisely your loyalty—exactly what I sought; my earlier words were only in jest."
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "That loyalty is exactly what I wanted; I was only jesting before."

sentences.zh: 待之彌厚，以為中常侍。

translations.literal: He treated Guang Zuo still more generously and appointed him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Guang Zuo even more warmly and made him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 翟遼遣其子釗寇陳、穎，朱序遣將軍秦膺擊走之。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao sent his son Zhao to raid Chen and Ying; Zhu Xu sent the general Qin Ying to strike and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao sent his son Zhao to raid Chen and Ying; Zhu Xu sent General Qin Ying, who beat them back.

sentences.zh: 秦主登立妃毛氏為皇后，勃海王懿為太弟。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng installed Lady Mao as empress and the Prince of Bohai, Yi, as Grand Younger Brother.
translations.idiomatic: Qin ruler Fu Deng made Lady Mao empress and Prince Fu Yi of Bohai Grand Younger Brother.

sentences.zh: 後，興之女也。

translations.literal: The empress was a daughter of Fu Xing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was Fu Xing's daughter.

sentences.zh: 遣使拜東海王纂為使持節、都督中外諸軍事、太師、領大司馬，封魯王，纂弟師奴為撫軍大將軍、并州牧，封朔方公。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to invest the Prince of Donghai, Zuan, with the staff of authority, command of all military affairs within and without, the title Grand Preceptor, and concurrent office as Grand Marshal, enfeoffing him as Prince of Lu; Zuan's younger brother Shinu was made General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Bing Province, enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to appoint Prince Fu Zuan of Donghai commander of all forces with the staff of authority, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Marshal, enfeoffing him as Prince of Lu; Zuan's brother Shinu became General Who Pacifies the Army and Governor of Bing, enfeoffed as Duke of Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 纂怒謂使者曰：「勃海王，先帝之子，南安王何以不立而自立乎？」

translations.literal: Zuan angrily told the envoy, "The Prince of Bohai is a son of the former emperor—why was the Prince of Nan'an not enthroned while he installs himself?"
translations.idiomatic: Zuan angrily told the envoy, "Prince Yi of Bohai is the late emperor's son—why enthrone Nan'an's prince while passing over him?"

sentences.zh: 長史王旅諫曰：「南安已立，理無中改；

translations.literal: The chief clerk Wang Lü remonstrated, "Nan'an is already enthroned; by principle there can be no reversal mid-course;
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Wang Lü urged, "Nan'an is already on the throne; the succession cannot be reopened;

sentences.zh: 今寇虜未滅，不可宗室之中自為仇敵也。」

translations.literal: now the enemy has not yet been destroyed—you must not make enemies of one another within the imperial clan."
translations.idiomatic: the foe is not yet beaten—you must not turn the clan against itself."

sentences.zh: 纂乃受命。

translations.literal: Zuan then accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan then accepted.

sentences.zh: 於是盧水胡彭沛谷、屠各董成、張龍世、新平羌雷惡地等皆附於篡，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Lushui Hu Peng Peigu, the Tuge Dong Cheng, Zhang Longshi, the Xiping Qiang Lei E'di, and others all attached themselves to Zuan, mustering more than a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Then Peng Peigu of the Lushui Hu, Dong Cheng of the Tuge, Zhang Longshi, Lei E'di of the Xiping Qiang, and others rallied to Zuan with more than a hundred thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇徙秦州豪傑三萬戶於安定。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang moved thirty thousand households of Qinzhou notables to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang relocated thirty thousand leading families from Qinzhou to Anding.

sentences.zh: 初，安次人齊涉聚眾八千餘家據新柵，降燕，燕主垂拜涉魏郡太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qi She of Anci gathered more than eight thousand households, seized Xinzha, and submitted to Yan; the Yan ruler Chui appointed She Administrator of Wei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qi She of Anci rallied more than eight thousand households, held Xinzha, and submitted to Yan; Murong Chui made him Administrator of Wei.

sentences.zh: 既而復叛，連張願，願自帥萬餘人進屯祝阿之甕口，招翟遼，共應涉。

translations.literal: Soon he rebelled again, linking with Zhang Yuan; Yuan himself led more than ten thousand men forward to encamp at Wengkou in Zhu'a, calling on Zhai Liao to join in supporting She.
translations.idiomatic: He soon rebelled again, allying with Zhang Yuan, who led more than ten thousand men to Wengkou near Zhu'a, summoned Zhai Liao, and acted with She.

sentences.zh: 高陽王隆言於垂曰：「新柵堅固，攻之未易猝拔。

translations.literal: The Prince of Gaoyang, Long, said to Chui, "Xinzha is stoutly fortified; it will not be easy to take it in a sudden assault.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Long of Gaoyang told Chui, "Xinzha is strong; a quick assault will not uproot it.

sentences.zh: 若久頓兵於其城下，張願擁帥流民，西引丁零，為患方深。

translations.literal: If we linger long beneath its walls, Zhang Yuan will gather displaced people and draw the Dingling from the west—the harm will grow deep.
translations.idiomatic: If we camp there too long, Zhang Yuan will rally refugees and pull Dingling allies from the west—the danger will deepen.

sentences.zh: 願眾雖多，然皆新附，未能力鬥。

translations.literal: Yuan's host is numerous, but all are newly attached and cannot fight hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan has numbers, but his men are new followers and will not fight hard.

sentences.zh: 因其自至，宜先擊之。

translations.literal: Since he has come of his own accord, we ought to strike him first.
translations.idiomatic: Since he has come to us, we should hit him first.

sentences.zh: 願父子恃其驍勇，必不肯避去，可一戰擒也。

translations.literal: Father and son Yuan trust in their fierceness and will surely not avoid battle; they can be seized in a single fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuans rely on their valor and will not slip away—we can take them in one battle.

sentences.zh: 願破，則涉自不能存矣。」

translations.literal: When Yuan is broken, She cannot survive on his own."
translations.idiomatic: Break Yuan, and She cannot hold out alone."

sentences.zh: 垂從之。

translations.literal: Chui followed this counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Chui agreed.

sentences.zh: 二月，遣范陽王德、陳留王紹、龍驤將軍張崇帥步騎二萬會隆擊願。

translations.literal: In the second month he sent the Prince of Fanyang, De, the Prince of Chenliu, Shao, and the Dragon-Cavalry General Zhang Chong with twenty thousand foot and horse to join Long in attacking Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he sent Princes Murong De of Fanyang and Murong Shao of Chenliu and Dragon-Cavalry General Zhang Chong with twenty thousand troops to join Long against Yuan.

sentences.zh: 軍至斗城，去甕口二十餘里，解鞍頓息。

translations.literal: The army reached Doucheng, more than twenty li from Wengkou, and loosened saddles to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Doucheng, a little over twenty li from Wengkou, and dismounted to rest.

sentences.zh: 願引兵奄至，燕人驚遽，德軍退走，隆勒兵不動。

translations.literal: Yuan led his troops in a sudden arrival; the Yan men were startled, De's army fell back in flight, but Long held his ranks unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan struck suddenly; the Yan troops panicked, De's wing broke and fled, but Long held his line.

sentences.zh: 願子龜出沖陳，隆遣左右王末逆擊，斬之。

translations.literal: Yuan's son Gui charged the line; Long sent his attendant Wang Mo to counterattack and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's son Gui charged the formation; Long sent Wang Mo, who cut him down.

sentences.zh: 隆徐進戰，願兵乃退。

translations.literal: Long advanced into battle at an easy pace, and Yuan's troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Long pressed forward steadily until Yuan's men gave way.

sentences.zh: 德行裡餘，復速兵還，與隆合，謂隆：「賊氣方銳，宜且緩之。」

translations.literal: After going more than a li, De hurried his troops back, rejoined Long, and said to him, "The enemy's spirit is still sharp—we ought to slacken for now."
translations.idiomatic: De had retreated a li or more, then rushed back to Long and said, "The enemy is still fierce—we should hold off."

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「願乘人不備，宜得大捷；

translations.literal: Long said, "Yuan took us unawares and ought to have won a great victory;
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "Yuan caught us off guard and should have won big;

sentences.zh: 而吾士卒皆以懸隔河津，勢迫之故，人思自戰，故能卻之。

translations.literal: yet our soldiers, cut off from the river crossing and pressed by circumstance, each wished to fight for himself, and so we could repulse them.
translations.idiomatic: but our men, cut off from the ford and cornered, each fought for his life—that is why we beat them back.

sentences.zh: 今賊不得利，氣竭勢衰，皆有進退之志，不能齊奮，宜亟待擊之。」

translations.literal: Now the enemy gained no advantage; their spirit is spent and their momentum faded—each has thoughts of advance or retreat and cannot charge together. We should press the attack at once."
translations.idiomatic: Now they have gained nothing; their spirit is spent and their momentum broken—each man is wavering and they cannot charge as one. We must strike while we can."

sentences.zh: 德曰：「吾唯卿所為耳。」

translations.literal: De said, "I will do only as you say."
translations.idiomatic: De said, "I leave it to you."

sentences.zh: 遂進，戰於甕口，大破之，斬首七千八百級，願脫身保三布口。

translations.literal: They advanced, fought at Wengkou, and routed the enemy utterly, taking seven thousand eight hundred heads; Yuan escaped and held Sanbukou.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced, fought at Wengkou, and routed Yuan, taking 7,800 heads; Yuan fled to Sanbukou.

sentences.zh: 燕人進軍歷城，青、兗、徐州郡縣壁壘多降。

translations.literal: The Yan army pressed on to Licheng; walled places in Qing, Yan, and Xu provinces mostly surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan army marched on Licheng, and fortified towns across Qing, Yan, and Xu largely submitted.

sentences.zh: 垂以陳留王紹為青州刺史，鎮歷地。

translations.literal: Chui appointed the Prince of Chenliu, Shao, Inspector of Qing Province and stationed him at Lidi.
translations.idiomatic: Chui made Prince Murong Shao of Chenliu Inspector of Qing and posted him at Lidi.

sentences.zh: 德等還師，新柵人冬鸞執涉送之。

translations.literal: As De and the others returned, Dong Luan of Xinzha seized She and sent him in.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march, Dong Luan of Xinzha seized She and handed him over.

sentences.zh: 垂誅涉父子，餘悉原之。

translations.literal: Chui executed She and his sons; all the rest were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Chui executed She and his sons and pardoned the rest.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦主登以竇沖為南秦州牧，楊定為益州牧，楊壁為司空、梁州牧，乞伏國仁為大將軍、大單于、苑川王。

translations.literal: In the third month the Qin ruler Deng appointed Dou Chong Governor of Southern Qinzhou, Yang Ding Governor of Yizhou, Yang Bi Minister of Works and Governor of Liangzhou, and Qifu Guoren Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Yuanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Fu Deng made Dou Chong Governor of Southern Qin, Yang Ding Governor of Yi, Yang Bi Minister of Works and Governor of Liang, and Qifu Guoren Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Yuanchuan.

sentences.zh: 燕上谷人王敏殺太守封戢，代郡人許謙逐太守賈閏，各以郡附劉顯。

translations.literal: Wang Min of Shanggu in Yan killed the Administrator Feng Ji; Xu Qian of Dai Commandery drove out the Administrator Jia Run; each surrendered his commandery to Liu Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Min of Shanggu killed Administrator Feng Ji; Xu Qian of Dai drove out Administrator Jia Run; each turned his commandery over to Liu Xian.

sentences.zh: 燕樂浪王溫為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Murong Wen, Prince of Lelang in Yan, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Right.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wen, Prince of Lelang, became Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the right.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊辰，尊帝母李氏為皇太妃，儀服如太后。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuchen, the emperor's mother Lady Li was honored as Grand Imperial Consort with rites and regalia like an empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's wuchen day, the emperor's mother Lady Li was honored as Grand Imperial Consort with the rites of an empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 後秦征西將軍姚碩德為楊定所逼，退過涇陽。

translations.literal: Yao Shuode, Later Qin's general who campaigns west, was pressed by Yang Ding and withdrew past Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin's western campaign general Yao Shuode, pressed by Yang Ding, fell back beyond Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 定與秦魯王纂共攻之，戰於涇陽，碩德大敗。

translations.literal: Ding and the Qin Prince of Lu, Zuan, attacked him together; they fought at Jingyang and Shuode was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ding and Qin Prince Fu Zuan of Lu attacked together; at Jingyang Shuode suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇自陰密救之，纂退屯敷陸。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang came from Yinmi to rescue him; Zuan withdrew and encamped at Fulu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang marched from Yinmi to relieve him; Zuan pulled back to Fulu.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂自碻磝還中山，慕容柔、慕容盛、慕容會來自長子。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui returned from Que'ao to Zhongshan; Murong Rou, Murong Sheng, and Murong Hui came from Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui returned from Que'ao to Zhongshan; Murong Rou, Murong Sheng, and Murong Hui arrived from Changzi.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，垂為之大赦。

translations.literal: On gengchen Chui proclaimed a general amnesty on their account.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he declared a general amnesty to mark their arrival.

sentences.zh: 垂問盛：「長子人情如何？

translations.literal: Chui asked Sheng, "How is sentiment at Changzi?
translations.idiomatic: Chui asked Sheng, "What is the mood in Changzi?

sentences.zh: 為可取乎？」

translations.literal: Can it be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Can we take it?"

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「西軍擾擾，人有東歸之志，陛下唯當修仁政以俟之耳。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "The western army is in turmoil; the people yearn to return east. Your Majesty need only cultivate benevolent rule and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "The western garrison is unsettled and the people long to come east. Your Majesty need only rule with benevolence and wait.

sentences.zh: 若大國一臨，必投戈而來，若孝子之歸慈父也。」

translations.literal: When the great state arrives, they will surely cast aside weapons and come, like a filial son returning to a loving father."
translations.idiomatic: When your great army appears, they will drop their weapons and come home like sons returning to a loving father."

sentences.zh: 垂悅。

translations.literal: Chui was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chui was delighted.

sentences.zh: 癸未，封柔為陽平王，盛為長樂公，會為清河公。

translations.literal: On guiwei he enfeoffed Rou as Prince of Yangping, Sheng as Duke of Changle, and Hui as Duke of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei he enfeoffed Rou as Prince of Yangping, Sheng as Duke of Changle, and Hui as Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 高平人翟暢執太守徐含遠，以郡降翟遼。

translations.literal: Zhai Chang of Gaoping seized the Administrator Xu Hanyuan and surrendered the commandery to Zhai Liao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Chang of Gaoping seized Administrator Xu Hanyuan and handed Gaoping to Zhai Liao.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂謂諸將曰：「遼以一城之眾，返覆三國之間，不可不討。」

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui told his generals, "Liao with the forces of a single city has shifted back and forth among three states—he cannot go unpunished."
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui told his generals, "With one city's strength Liao has played all three kingdoms off one another—he must be punished."

sentences.zh: 五月，以章武王宙監中外諸軍事，輔太子寶守中山，垂自帥諸將南攻遼，以太原王楷為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he appointed the Prince of Zhangwu, Zhou, to oversee all military affairs within and without, to assist the crown prince Bao in holding Zhongshan, while Chui himself led the generals south to attack Liao, with the Prince of Taiyuan, Kai, as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he put Prince Murong Zhou of Zhangwu in charge of all forces to assist Crown Prince Bao at Zhongshan, while he led the army south against Liao with Prince Murong Kai of Taiyuan as vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 遼眾皆燕、趙之人，聞楷至，皆曰：「太原王子，吾之父母也！」

translations.literal: Liao's troops were all men of Yan and Zhao; when they heard Kai had come, they said, "The Prince of Taiyuan is our father and mother!"
translations.idiomatic: Liao's men were Yan and Zhao natives; hearing Kai had come, they cried, "The Prince of Taiyuan is our father and mother!"

sentences.zh: 相遇歸之。

translations.literal: Meeting him, they went over to him.
translations.idiomatic: They went over to him on sight.

sentences.zh: 遼懼，遣使請降。

translations.literal: Liao was afraid and sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Liao, afraid, sent envoys to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 垂以遼為徐州牧，封河南公；

translations.literal: Chui made Liao Governor of Xuzhou and enfeoffed him as Duke of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: Chui made him Governor of Xu and Duke of Henan;

sentences.zh: 前至黎陽，受降而還。

translations.literal: advancing to Liyang, accepting the surrender, and returning.
translations.idiomatic: advanced to Liyang, accepted his submission, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 井陘人賈鮑，招引北山丁零翟遙等五千餘人，夜襲中山，隱其外郭。

translations.literal: Jia Bao of Jingxing drew more than five thousand Dingling of the northern hills led by Zhai Yao and others, raided Zhongshan by night, and concealed themselves outside the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Bao of Jingxing rallied more than five thousand northern Dingling under Zhai Yao, raided Zhongshan by night, and hid outside the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 章武王宙以奇兵出其外，太子寶鼓噪於內。

translations.literal: The Prince of Zhangwu, Zhou, led picked troops out beyond them, while the crown prince Bao beat drums and shouted within.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Zhou of Zhangwu led picked troops outside while Crown Prince Bao drummed and shouted within.

sentences.zh: 合擊，大破之，盡俘其眾，唯遙、鮑單馬走免。

translations.literal: Striking together, they routed the raiders utterly and captured the whole host; only Yao and Bao escaped on lone horses.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking from both sides, they routed the raiders and took every man; only Yao and Bao escaped alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 劉顯地廣兵強，雄於北方。

translations.literal: Liu Xian's territory was broad and his army strong; he dominated the north.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xian held broad lands and a strong army and was the power of the north.

sentences.zh: 會其兄弟乖爭，魏長史張兗言於魏王珪曰：「顯志在併吞，今不乘其內潰而取之，必為後患。

translations.literal: It happened that his brothers were at odds; the Wei chief clerk Zhang Gun said to the Wei king Gui, "Xian's aim is to swallow all—if we do not seize him while he is riven within, he will surely become a later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Just then his brothers fell out; Wei chief clerk Zhang Gun told King Tuoba Gui, "Xian means to swallow everything—if we do not strike while he is split within, he will trouble us later.

sentences.zh: 然吾不能獨克，請與燕共攻之。」

translations.literal: Yet we cannot overcome him alone; I ask to attack him together with Yan."
translations.idiomatic: We cannot beat him alone—I ask that we attack with Yan."

sentences.zh: 珪從之，復遣安同乞師於燕。

translations.literal: Gui agreed and again sent An Tong to beg troops from Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui agreed and again sent An Tong to ask Yan for troops.

sentences.zh: 詔征會稽處士戴逵，逵累辭不就；

translations.literal: An edict summoned the recluse Dai Kui of Kuaiji; Kui repeatedly declined and would not come;
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned the recluse Dai Kui of Kuaiji; Kui repeatedly refused;

sentences.zh: 郡縣敦逼不已，逵逃匿於吳。

translations.literal: the commanderies and counties pressed him without cease, and Kui fled into hiding in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: local officials kept pressing him, and he hid in Wu.

sentences.zh: 謝玄上疏曰：「逵自求其志，今王命未回，將罹風霜之患。

translations.literal: Xie Xuan submitted a memorial saying, "Kui seeks his own path; now the royal command has not been withdrawn, and he will suffer the hardship of wind and frost.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xuan memorialized, "Kui is following his own calling; yet the summons still stands and he will suffer exposure and hardship.

sentences.zh: 陛下既已愛而器之，亦宜使其身名並存；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has already cherished and valued him—you ought also to let both his person and his name survive;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty already values him—you should let both the man and his reputation endure;

sentences.zh: 請絕召命。」

translations.literal: I ask that the summons be revoked."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the summons be withdrawn."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 逵，之兄也。

translations.literal: Kui was Xuan's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was Xuan's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 秦主登以其兄同成為司徒、守尚書令，封穎川王；

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng appointed his elder brother Tongcheng Minister of Education and acting Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffing him as Prince of Yingchuan;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng made his elder brother Fu Tongcheng Minister of Education and acting Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffing him as Prince of Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 弟廣為中書監，封安成王；

translations.literal: his younger brother Guang was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Prince of Ancheng;
translations.idiomatic: his brother Guang became Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Ancheng;

sentences.zh: 子崇為尚書左僕射，封東平王。

translations.literal: his son Chong was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Left, and enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: his son Fu Chong was made Vice Director on the left and Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂自黎陽還中山。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui returned from Liyang to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui returned from Liyang to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 吳深殺燕清河太守丁國，章武人王祖殺太守白欽，勃海人張申據高城以叛；

translations.literal: Wu Shen killed Ding Guo, Administrator of Qinghe in Yan; Wang Zu of Zhangwu killed the Administrator Bai Qin; Zhang Shen of Bohai seized Gaocheng and rebelled;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shen killed Yan's Qinghe administrator Ding Guo; Wang Zu of Zhangwu killed Administrator Bai Qin; Zhang Shen of Bohai seized Gaocheng and rebelled;

sentences.zh: 燕主垂命樂浪王溫討之。

translations.literal: the Yan ruler Chui ordered the Prince of Lelang, Wen, to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui sent Prince Murong Wen of Lelang against them.

sentences.zh: 苑川王國仁帥騎三萬襲鮮卑大人密貴、裕苟、提倫三部於六泉。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuanchuan, Guoren, led thirty thousand horse to strike the three Xianbei chieftains Migui, Yugou, and Tilun at Liuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qifu Guoren of Yuanchuan led thirty thousand cavalry against the Xianbei chiefs Migui, Yugou, and Tilun at Liuquan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，與沒弈干、金熙戰於渴渾川。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, he fought Moyigan and Jin Xi at Kehun River.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, he fought Moyigan and Jin Xi on the Kehun River.

sentences.zh: 沒弈干、金熙大敗，三部皆降。

translations.literal: Moyigan and Jin Xi were utterly defeated, and all three tribes surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Moyigan and Jin Xi were routed, and all three tribes submitted.

sentences.zh: 秦主登軍於瓦亭，後秦主萇攻彭沛谷堡，拔之，谷奔杏城。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng encamped at Wating; the Later Qin ruler Chang attacked Peng Peigu's fortress, took it, and Peigu fled to Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng camped at Wating; Yao Chang of Later Qin took Peng Peigu's fortress; Peigu fled to Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 萇還陰密，以太子興鎮長安。

translations.literal: Chang returned to Yinmi and stationed the crown prince Xing at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chang returned to Yinmi and left Crown Prince Yao Xing at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 燕趙王麟討王敏於上谷，斬之。

translations.literal: The Yan Prince of Zhao, Lin, attacked Wang Min at Shanggu and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Lin of Zhao attacked Wang Min in Shanggu and killed him.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰獻馬於燕，劉顯掠之。

translations.literal: Liu Weichen presented horses to Yan; Liu Xian plundered them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen sent horses as tribute to Yan; Liu Xian seized them.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂怒，遣太原王楷將兵助趙王麟擊顯，大破之。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui was angry and sent the Prince of Taiyuan, Kai, with troops to assist the Prince of Zhao, Lin, in attacking Xian; they routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, enraged, sent Prince Murong Kai of Taiyuan to help Prince Murong Lin of Zhao; they crushed Xian.

sentences.zh: 顯奔馬邑西山，魏王引兵會麟擊顯於彌澤，又破之。

translations.literal: Xian fled to the western hills of Mayi; the Wei king led troops to join Lin in attacking Xian at Mize and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: Xian fled to the western hills of Mayi; King Tuoba Gui joined Lin at Mize and beat him again.

sentences.zh: 顯奔西密，麟悉收其部眾，獲馬牛羊以千萬數。

translations.literal: Xian fled to Ximi; Lin gathered all his followers and took horses, cattle, and sheep numbering in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Xian fled to Ximi; Lin took all his followers and livestock by the millions.

sentences.zh: 呂光將彭晃，徐炅攻張大豫於臨洮，破之。

translations.literal: Lü Guang's generals Peng Huang and Xu Jiong attacked Zhang Dayu at Lintao and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang's generals Peng Huang and Xu Jiong defeated Zhang Dayu at Lintao.

sentences.zh: 大豫奔廣武，王穆奔建康。

translations.literal: Dayu fled to Guangwu; Wang Mu fled to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Dayu fled to Guangwu; Wang Mu fled to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 八月，廣武人執大豫送姑臧，斬之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the people of Guangwu seized Dayu and sent him to Guzang, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Guangwu men seized Dayu, sent him to Guzang, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 穆襲據酒泉，自稱大將軍、涼州牧。

translations.literal: Mu seized Jiuquan and styled himself Grand General and Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mu seized Jiuquan and proclaimed himself Grand General and Governor of Liang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，立皇子德宗為太子，大赦。

translations.literal: On xinsi the prince Dezong was installed as crown prince and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the court made Prince Dezong crown prince and declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂立劉顯弟可泥為烏桓王，以撫其眾，徙八千餘落於中山。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui installed Liu Xian's younger brother Keni as Prince of the Wuhuan to pacify his followers and moved more than eight thousand households to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui made Liu Xian's brother Keni Wuhuan king to pacify his people and moved more than eight thousand households to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 秦馮翊太守蘭櫝帥眾二萬自頻陽入和寧，與魯王纂謀攻長安。

translations.literal: Lan Han, Administrator of Fenyang in Qin, led twenty thousand men from Pinyang into He'ning and plotted with the Prince of Lu, Zuan, to attack Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han, Qin administrator of Fenyang, led twenty thousand men from Pinyang into He'ning to join Prince Fu Zuan of Lu in an attack on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 纂弟師奴勸纂稱尊號，纂不從。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Shinu urged Zuan to take the imperial title; Zuan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's brother Shinu urged him to proclaim himself emperor; Zuan refused.

sentences.zh: 師奴殺纂而代之，櫝遂與師奴絕。

translations.literal: Shinu killed Zuan and replaced him; Lan Han then broke with Shinu.
translations.idiomatic: Shinu killed Zuan and seized his place; Lan Han then broke with Shinu.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永攻櫝，櫝遣使請救於後秦。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Yong attacked Lan Han; Han sent envoys to beg rescue from Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan ruler Murong Yong attacked Lan Han, who asked Later Qin for help.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇欲自救之，尚書令姚旻，左僕射尹緯曰：「苻登近在瓦亭，將乘虛襲吾後。」

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang wished to rescue him himself. The Director of the Masters of Writing Yao Min and the Vice Director on the left Yin Wei said, "Fu Deng is near at Wating and will seize the moment to strike our rear."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang meant to go in person. Director Yao Min and Vice Director Yin Wei said, "Fu Deng is at Wating and will strike our rear while we are away."

sentences.zh: 萇曰；

translations.literal: Chang said:
translations.idiomatic: Chang said:

sentences.zh: 「苻登眾盛，非旦夕可制；

translations.literal: "Fu Deng's host is strong and cannot be mastered in a day or a night;
translations.idiomatic: "Deng's army is large and cannot be crushed overnight;

sentences.zh: 登遲重少決，必不能輕軍深入。

translations.literal: Deng is slow, heavy, and seldom decisive—he surely cannot lead a light force deep in.
translations.idiomatic: Deng is slow and hesitant and will not march deep with a light force.

sentences.zh: 比兩月間，吾必破賊而返，登雖至，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Within two months I will surely break the enemy and return; even if Deng comes, he can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: In two months I will break the enemy and return; even if Deng comes, he can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 九月，萇軍於泥源。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Chang encamped at Niyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Chang camped at Niyuan.

sentences.zh: 師奴逆戰，大敗，亡奔鮮卑。

translations.literal: Shinu met him in battle, was utterly defeated, and fled to the Xianbei.
translations.idiomatic: Shinu fought him, was routed, and fled to the Xianbei.

sentences.zh: 後秦盡收其眾，屠各董成等皆降。

translations.literal: Later Qin gathered all his followers; Dong Cheng of the Tuge and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin took all his troops; Dong Cheng of the Tuge and others submitted.

sentences.zh: 秦主登進據胡空堡，戎、夏歸之者十餘萬。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng advanced and seized Hukong Fortress; more than a hundred thousand Rong and Xia came over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng took Hukong Fortress; more than a hundred thousand tribal followers joined him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，翟遼復叛燕，遣兵與王祖、張申寇抄清河、平原。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Zhai Liao rebelled against Yan again and sent troops with Wang Zu and Zhang Shen to raid Qinghe and Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Zhai Liao rebelled again and sent troops with Wang Zu and Zhang Shen to raid Qinghe and Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇進擊西燕主永於河西，永走。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang advanced to attack the Western Yan ruler Yong west of the river; Yong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang attacked Murong Yong of Western Yan west of the river; Yong fled.

sentences.zh: 蘭櫝復列兵拒守，萇攻之，十二月，禽櫝，遂如杏城。

translations.literal: Lan Han again drew up his troops to resist; Chang attacked him, and in the twelfth month captured Han and then went on to Xingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han rallied to resist; Chang attacked, and in the twelfth month captured him and marched on to Xingcheng.

sentences.zh: 後泰姚方成攻秦雍州刺史徐嵩壘，拔之，執嵩而數之。

translations.literal: Yao Fangcheng of Later Qin attacked the fortress of Xu Song, Qin Governor of Yong Province, took it, seized Song, and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin's Yao Fangcheng took the fortress of Qin Yong governor Xu Song, seized him, and rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 嵩罵曰：「汝姚萇罪當萬死，苻黃眉欲斬之，先帝止之。

translations.literal: Song cursed him, saying, "You, Yao Chang, deserve ten thousand deaths. Fu Huangmei wished to behead you, but the former emperor stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Song cursed him: "You, Yao Chang, deserve death ten thousand times over. Fu Huangmei wanted you beheaded, but the late emperor spared you.

sentences.zh: 授任內外，榮寵極矣。

translations.literal: He gave you posts within and without; honor and favor reached their height.
translations.idiomatic: He gave you office at court and in the field—honor beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 曾不如犬馬識所養之恩，親為大逆。

translations.literal: You were not even as a dog or horse that knows the kindness of its keeper—you personally committed great treason.
translations.idiomatic: You were less grateful than a dog or horse that knows its master's care, and you rebelled with your own hands.

sentences.zh: 汝羌輩豈可以人理期也！

translations.literal: How can one expect human reason from you Qiang!
translations.idiomatic: What human decency can one expect from you Qiang!

sentences.zh: 何不速殺我，早見先帝取姚萇於地下治之！」

translations.literal: Why not kill me quickly, so I may soon see the former emperor take Yao Chang below and judge him!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill me now, so I may see the late emperor drag Yao Chang below to answer for this!"

sentences.zh: 方成怒，三斬嵩，悉坑其士卒，以妻子賞軍。

translations.literal: Fangcheng in anger hacked Song three times, buried all his soldiers alive, and gave their wives and children to the army as rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Fangcheng hacked him three times in rage, buried all his men alive, and gave their families to the troops as booty.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇掘秦主堅屍，鞭撻無數，剝衣裸形，薦之以棘，坎土而埋之。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang dug up the corpse of the Qin ruler Jian, flogged it countless times, stripped it naked, laid thorns beneath it, and buried it in a pit of earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang dug up Fu Jian's corpse, flogged it endlessly, stripped it bare, laid it on thorns, and buried it in a shallow pit.

sentences.zh: 涼州大饑，米斗直錢五百，人相食，死者太半。

translations.literal: Liangzhou suffered great famine; grain sold for five hundred cash per dou; men ate one another, and more than half died.
translations.idiomatic: Liang suffered famine; grain cost five hundred cash per dou; people ate one another, and more than half the population died.

sentences.zh: 呂光西平太守康寧自稱匈奴王，殺河湟太守強禧以叛。

translations.literal: Kang Ning, Administrator of Xiping under Lü Guang, styled himself King of the Xiongnu, killed the Administrator of Hehuang Qiang Xi, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Ning, Lü Guang's Xiping administrator, proclaimed himself Xiongnu king, killed Hehuang administrator Qiang Xi, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 張掖太守彭晃亦叛，東結康寧，西通王穆。

translations.literal: Peng Huang, Administrator of Zhangye, also rebelled, linking east with Kang Ning and west with Wang Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangye administrator Peng Huang rebelled too, allying east with Kang Ning and west with Wang Mu.

sentences.zh: 光欲自擊晃，諸將皆曰：「今康寧在南，伺釁而動。

translations.literal: Guang wished to strike Huang himself; all the generals said, "Kang Ning is now in the south, watching for an opening to move.
translations.idiomatic: Guang wanted to attack Huang himself; his generals said, "Kang Ning is in the south, waiting for an opening.

sentences.zh: 若晃、穆未誅，康寧復至，進退狼狽，勢必大危。」

translations.literal: If Huang and Mu are not executed before Ning comes again, we will be caught between advance and retreat in distress—the danger will be great."
translations.idiomatic: If Huang and Mu are not dealt with before Ning strikes, we will be caught between enemies and in grave danger."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「實如卿言。

translations.literal: Guang said, "It is truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 然我今不往，是坐待其來也。

translations.literal: Yet if I do not go now, I am simply sitting and waiting for them to come.
translations.idiomatic: But if I stay here, I am only waiting for them to come.

sentences.zh: 若三寇連兵，東西交至，則城外皆非吾有，大事去矣。

translations.literal: If the three rebels join forces and attack from east and west together, then nothing outside the walls will be ours and the great enterprise is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If all three unite and hit us from east and west, everything beyond the walls is lost and the cause is finished.

sentences.zh: 今晃初叛，與寧、穆情契未密，出其倉猝，取之差易耳。」

translations.literal: Now Huang has just rebelled; his bond with Ning and Mu is not yet close—strike him in sudden haste and he will be comparatively easy to take."
translations.idiomatic: Huang has only just rebelled; his ties with Ning and Mu are not firm yet—strike suddenly and he will be easy to take."

sentences.zh: 乃自帥騎三萬，倍道兼行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he himself led thirty thousand horse by forced marches day and night.
translations.idiomatic: He led thirty thousand cavalry by forced march.

sentences.zh: 既至，攻之二旬，拔其城，誅晃。

translations.literal: When he arrived he attacked for twenty days, took the city, and executed Huang.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged twenty days, took the city, and executed Huang.

sentences.zh: 初，王穆起兵，遣使招敦煌處士郭瑀，運粟三萬石以餉之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Mu raised troops, he sent envoys to recruit the recluse Guo Yu of Dunhuang and transported thirty thousand shi of grain to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mu first rose, he summoned the recluse Guo Yu of Dunhuang and sent thirty thousand shi of grain as support.

sentences.zh: 穆以瑀為太府左長史、軍師將軍，嘏為敦煌太守。

translations.literal: Mu made Yu Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Treasury and General of the Army Staff; Jia was made Administrator of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Mu made Yu Grand Treasury chief clerk on the left and staff general, and Jia administrator of Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 既而穆聽讒言，引兵攻嘏，瑀諫不聽，出城大哭，舉手謝城曰：「吾不復見汝矣！」

translations.literal: Soon Mu listened to slander, led troops to attack Jia, and Yu remonstrated in vain; Yu went outside the city and wept aloud, raising his hands to bid the city farewell: "I shall not see you again!"
translations.idiomatic: Then Mu believed slander and attacked Jia; Yu protested in vain, went outside the walls, wept, and raised his hands to the city: "I shall not see you again!"

sentences.zh: 還而引被覆面，不與人言，不食而卒。

translations.literal: Returning, he drew a coverlet over his face, spoke to no one, ate nothing, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He returned, covered his face, spoke to no one, refused food, and died.

sentences.zh: 呂光聞之，曰：「二虜相攻，此成擒也，不可以憚屢戰之勞而失永逸之機也。」

translations.literal: When Lü Guang heard this he said, "The two rebels are attacking each other—this means they can be captured. One must not shrink from the weariness of repeated battles and lose the chance of lasting peace."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang said, "The two rebels are fighting each other—we can take them both. We must not shrink from battle and miss a lasting victory."

sentences.zh: 遂帥步騎二萬攻酒泉，克之，進屯涼興；

translations.literal: Thereupon he led twenty thousand foot and horse to attack Jiuquan, took it, and advanced to encamp at Liangxing;
translations.idiomatic: He led twenty thousand troops against Jiuquan, took it, and camped at Liangxing;

sentences.zh: 穆引兵東還，未至，眾潰，穆單騎走，騂馬令郭文斬其首送之。

translations.literal: Mu led his troops back east; before he arrived his host collapsed; Mu fled alone on horseback, and Guo Wen, Magistrate of Xingma, beheaded him and sent the head in.
translations.idiomatic: Mu marched east, but his army collapsed before he arrived; he fled alone, and Xingma magistrate Guo Wen beheaded him and sent the head to Guang.

sentences.zh: 列宗孝武皇帝中之下太元十三年（

translations.literal: Middle and lower portion of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the thirteenth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: From the middle and latter part of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the thirteenth year of the Taiyuan era (

sentences.zh: 戊子，公元三八八年）

translations.literal: wuzi, corresponding to the year 388 CE).
translations.idiomatic: wuzi, corresponding to 388 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，康樂獻武公謝玄卒。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Xie Xuan, Duke of Kangle and Marquis of Xianwu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Xie Xuan, Duke of Kangle, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，秦主登軍朝那，後秦主萇軍武都。

translations.literal: In the second month the Qin ruler Deng encamped at Chaona and the Later Qin ruler Chang at Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Fu Deng camped at Chaona and Yao Chang at Wudu.

sentences.zh: 翟遼遣司馬眭瓊詣燕謝罪；

translations.literal: Zhai Liao sent the Major Sui Qiong to Yan to apologize;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao sent Major Sui Qiong to Yan to apologize;

sentences.zh: 燕主垂以其數反覆，斬瓊以絕之。

translations.literal: the Yan ruler Chui, because of his repeated shifts, beheaded Qiong to break with him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, weary of his repeated betrayals, beheaded Qiong to cut ties.

sentences.zh: 遼乃自稱魏天王，改元建光，置百官。

translations.literal: Liao then styled himself Heavenly King of Wei, changed the era name to Jianguang, and established the full bureaucracy.
translations.idiomatic: Liao then proclaimed himself Heavenly King of Wei, adopted the era name Jianguang, and set up a full court.

sentences.zh: 燕青州刺史陳留王紹為平原太守辟閭渾所逼，退屯黃巾固。

translations.literal: Murong Shao, Prince of Chenliu and Inspector of Qing Province in Yan, was pressed by Bi Lü Hun, Administrator of Pingyuan, and withdrew to encamp at Huangjin Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Qing inspector Prince Murong Shao of Chenliu was driven by Pingyuan administrator Bi Lü Hun to withdraw to Huangjin Fort.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂更以紹為徐州刺史。

translations.literal: The Yan ruler Chui reassigned Shao as Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui reassigned Shao as Inspector of Xu.

sentences.zh: 渾，蔚之子也。

translations.literal: Hun was the son of Bi Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was Bi Wei's son.

sentences.zh: 因苻氏亂，據齊地來降。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of the chaos of the Fu clan, he held Qi territory and came over in submission.
translations.idiomatic: He had seized Qi during the Fu clan's collapse and then submitted to Yan.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙亥，燕主垂以太子寶錄尚書事，授之以政，自總大綱而已。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yihai, the Yan ruler Chui had the crown prince Bao record affairs of the Masters of Writing, entrusted him with government, and himself held only the great outlines.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yihai, Murong Chui put Crown Prince Bao in charge of the Masters of Writing, handed him the administration, and kept only the broad direction himself.

sentences.zh: 燕趙麟擊許謙，破之，謙奔西燕。

translations.literal: Murong Lin of Yan attacked Xu Qian, defeated him, and Qian fled to Western Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin of Yan defeated Xu Qian, who fled to Western Yan.

sentences.zh: 遂廢代郡，悉徙其民於龍城。

translations.literal: He then abolished Dai Commandery and moved all its people to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished Dai commandery and moved all its people to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 呂光之定涼州也，杜進功居多。

translations.literal: When Lü Guang pacified Liangzhou, Du Jin's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Guang pacified Liang, Du Jin had done the most.

sentences.zh: 光以為武威太守，貴寵用事，群僚莫及。

translations.literal: Guang made him Administrator of Wuwei; honored and favored, he held power, and none among the officials could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang made him Wuwei administrator; favored above all, he dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 光甥石聰自關中來，光問之曰：「中州人言我為政何如？」

translations.literal: Guang's nephew Shi Cong came from the Guanzhong region; Guang asked him, "What do the central provinces say of my governance?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang's nephew Shi Cong came from Guanzhong; Guang asked, "What do people in the central provinces say of my rule?"

sentences.zh: 聰曰：「但聞有杜進耳，不聞有舅。」

translations.literal: Cong said, "They speak only of Du Jin—they do not speak of an uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Cong said, "They speak only of Du Jin—not of an uncle."

sentences.zh: 光由是忌進而殺之。

translations.literal: Because of this Guang grew jealous of Jin and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, jealous, killed him.

sentences.zh: 光與群寮宴，語及政事，參軍京兆段業曰：「明公用法太峻。」

translations.literal: At a banquet with his officials Guang spoke of government; the staff officer Duan Ye of Jingzhao said, "My lord's use of law is too severe."
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Guang spoke of government; staff officer Duan Ye of Jingzhao said, "My lord's laws are too harsh."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「吳起無恩而楚強，商殃嚴刑而秦興。」

translations.literal: Guang said, "Wu Qi showed no kindness yet Chu grew strong; Shang Yang used harsh punishments yet Qin rose."
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Wu Qi was ruthless yet Chu grew strong; Shang Yang was severe yet Qin rose."

sentences.zh: 業曰：「起喪其身，鞅亡其家，皆殘酷之致也。

translations.literal: Ye said, "Qi lost his own life; Yang lost his whole house—both outcomes of cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "Qi died for it; Yang's house was destroyed—both paid for cruelty.

sentences.zh: 明公方開建大業，景行堯、舜，猶懼不濟，乃慕起、鞅之為治，豈此州士女所望哉？」

translations.literal: My lord is just now founding a great enterprise and taking Yao and Shun as your model, yet still fear you may not succeed—and you admire the governance of Qi and Yang. Is this what the men and women of this province hope for?"
translations.idiomatic: You are founding a great enterprise and mean to follow Yao and Shun, yet still fear failure—and you admire Qi and Yang? Is that what the people of this province want?"

sentences.zh: 光改容謝之。

translations.literal: Guang changed expression and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang changed expression and apologized.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，戊午，以朱序為都督司、雍、梁、秦四州諸軍事、雍州刺史，戍洛陽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on wuwu, Zhu Xu was made Commander of all military affairs in Si, Yong, Liang, and Qin provinces and Governor of Yong, garrisoning Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the fourth month's wuwu day, Zhu Xu was made commander of Si, Yong, Liang, and Qin and Governor of Yong, posted at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 以譙王恬代為都督兗、冀、幽、并諸軍事、青、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince Tian of Qiao was appointed in his place Commander of military affairs in Yan, Ji, You, and Bing and Inspector of Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Tian of Qiao replaced him as commander of Yan, Ji, You, and Bing and Inspector of Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 苑川王國仁破鮮卑越質叱黎於平襄，獲其子詰歸。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuanchuan, Guoren, defeated the Xianbei Yuezhi Chili at Pingxiang and captured his son Jiegui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qifu Guoren of Yuanchuan defeated the Xianbei Yuezhi Chili at Pingxiang and captured his son Jiegui.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，燕主垂立夫人段氏為皇后，以太子寶領大單于。

translations.literal: On dinghai the Yan ruler Chui installed Lady Duan as empress and had the crown prince Bao take the title Grand Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Murong Chui made Lady Duan empress and put Crown Prince Bao in charge as Grand Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 段氏，右光祿大夫儀之女；

translations.literal: Lady Duan was the daughter of the Right Grandee of Splendid Happiness Yi;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Duan was the daughter of Right Grand Master Murong Yi;

sentences.zh: 其妹適范陽王德。

translations.literal: her younger sister was married to the Prince of Fanyang, De.
translations.idiomatic: her sister was married to Prince Murong De of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 儀，寶之舅也。

translations.literal: Yi was Bao's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was Bao's uncle on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 追謚前妃段氏為成昭皇后。

translations.literal: The former consort Lady Duan was posthumously titled Empress Chengzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The late consort Lady Duan was posthumously titled Empress Chengzhao.

sentences.zh: 五月，秦太弟懿卒，謚曰獻哀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the Qin Grand Younger Brother Yi died; his posthumous title was Xian'ai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Qin Grand Younger Brother Fu Yi died; he was posthumously titled Xian'ai.

sentences.zh: 翟遼徙屯滑台。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao moved his encampment to Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao moved his camp to Huatai.

sentences.zh: 六月，苑川王乞伏國仁卒，謚曰宣烈，廟號烈祖。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the Prince of Yuanchuan, Qifu Guoren, died; his posthumous title was Xuanlie, his temple name Liezu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Prince Qifu Guoren of Yuanchuan died; he was posthumously titled Xuanlie, with the temple name Liezu.

sentences.zh: 其子公府尚幼，群下推國仁弟乾歸為大都督、大將軍、大單于、河南王，大赦，改元太初。

translations.literal: His son Gongfu was still young; the subordinates raised Guoren's younger brother Qian'gui to Great Governor-General, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Henan, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Taichu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongfu was still a child, so the court raised Guoren's younger brother Qifu Qian'gui to Great Governor-General, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Henan, declared a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Taichu.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪破庫莫奚於弱落水南。

translations.literal: The Wei king, Tuoba Gui, defeated the Kumo Xi south of the Ruoshui River.
translations.idiomatic: King Tuoba Gui of Wei defeated the Kumo Xi south of the Ruoshui River.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，庫莫奚復襲魏營，珪又破之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Kumo Xi again raided the Wei camp; Gui defeated them once more.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Kumo Xi raided the Wei camp again; Gui routed them a second time.

sentences.zh: 庫莫奚者，本屬宇文部，與契丹同類而異種，其先皆為燕王皝所破，徙居松漠之間。

translations.literal: The Kumo Xi had originally belonged to the Yuwen tribe; they were of the same kind as the Khitan but a different branch. Their forebears had all been defeated by Murong Huang, Prince of Yan, and were moved to dwell among the pine deserts.
translations.idiomatic: The Kumo Xi had originally been part of the Yuwen tribe—kin to the Khitan but a separate people. Their ancestors had all been broken by Murong Huang of Yan and resettled in the pine deserts.

sentences.zh: 秦、後秦自春相持，屢戰，互有勝負，至是各解歸。

translations.literal: Former Qin and Later Qin had faced each other since spring, fighting repeatedly with alternating victories and defeats; by this time each side withdrew homeward.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin and Later Qin had been locked in stalemate since spring, clashing again and again with no clear winner; now each army went home.

sentences.zh: 關西豪傑以後秦久無成功，多去而附秦。

translations.literal: The stalwarts of western Guan, seeing that Later Qin had long failed to achieve success, for the most part left to join Former Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Later Qin had accomplished little for so long, many western Guan leaders deserted it for Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 河南王乾歸立其妻邊氏為王后；

translations.literal: The Prince of Henan, Qian'gui, installed his wife Lady Bian as queen;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qifu Qian'gui of Henan made his wife Lady Bian queen;

sentences.zh: 置百官，仿漢制，以南川侯出連乞都為丞相，梁州刺史悌眷為御史大夫，金城邊芮為左長史，東秦州刺史秘宜為右長史，武始翟勍為左司馬，略陽王松壽為主簿，從弟軻彈為梁州牧，弟益州為秦州牧，屈眷為河州牧。

translations.literal: he established the hundred offices, following the Han model: Marquis Chulian Qidu of Southern Chuan was made Chancellor; Tipan, Inspector of Liangzhou, Grand Censor; Bian Rui of Jincheng, Left Chief Clerk; Miyi, Inspector of Eastern Qinzhou, Right Chief Clerk; Zhai Jing of Wushi, Left Major; Prince Songshou of Lueyang, Registrar; his younger cousin Ke Dan, Governor of Liangzhou; his younger brother Yizhou, Governor of Qinzhou; and Qujuan, Governor of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: he set up a full bureaucracy on the Han model, appointing Marquis Chulian Qidu of Southern Chuan Chancellor; Tipan, Inspector of Liang, Grand Censor; Bian Rui of Jincheng, Left Chief Clerk; Miyi, Inspector of Eastern Qin, Right Chief Clerk; Zhai Jing of Wushi, Left Major; Prince Songshou of Lueyang, Registrar; his cousin Ke Dan, Governor of Liang; his brother Yizhou, Governor of Qin; and Qujuan, Governor of He.

sentences.zh: 八月，秦主登立子崇為皇太子，弁為南安王，尚為北海王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Qin ruler Deng installed his son Chong as crown prince, made Bian Prince of Nan'an, and Shang Prince of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Former Qin ruler Fu Deng made his son Chong crown prince, Fu Bian Prince of Nan'an, and Fu Shang Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 燕護軍將軍平幼會章武王宙討吳深，破之，深走保繹幕。

translations.literal: The Yan Protector-General Ping You joined Prince Murong Zhou of Zhangwu to attack Wu Shen, defeated him, and Shen fled to hold Yimuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Protector-General Ping You and Prince Murong Zhou of Zhangwu attacked Wu Shen, routed him, and Shen fled to hold Yimuo.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪密有圖燕之志，遣九原公儀奉使至中山，燕主垂詰之曰：「魏王何以不自來？」

translations.literal: The Wei king, Tuoba Gui, secretly harbored designs on Yan and sent Duke Tuoba Yi of Jiuyuan as envoy to Zhongshan. The Yan ruler Chui interrogated him, saying, "Why does the Wei king not come himself?"
translations.idiomatic: King Tuoba Gui of Wei secretly planned against Yan and sent Duke Tuoba Yi of Jiuyuan as envoy to Zhongshan. Murong Chui, lord of Yan, demanded, "Why doesn't the Wei king come in person?"

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「先王與燕並事晉室，世為兄弟，臣今奉使，於理未失。」

translations.literal: Yi said, "The late king and Yan both served the Jin house, brothers generation after generation. As your servant I come on embassy—in principle nothing is amiss."
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied, "The late king and Yan both served the Jin court as brothers generation after generation. I come as envoy—nothing improper in that."

sentences.zh: 垂曰：「吾今威加四海，豈得以昔日為比！」

translations.literal: Chui said, "My authority now fills the four seas—how can that be measured against former days!"
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "My power now spans the four seas—how can you compare that with the old days!"

sentences.zh: 儀曰：「燕若不修德禮，欲以兵威自強，此乃將帥之事，非使臣所知也。」

translations.literal: Yi said, "If Yan will not cultivate virtue and propriety but seeks strength through armed might, that is the business of generals—not what this envoy is here to discuss."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "If Yan neglects virtue and ceremony and tries to grow strong by force of arms, that is generals' business—not mine as envoy."

sentences.zh: 儀還，言於珪曰；

translations.literal: When Yi returned he reported to Gui:
translations.idiomatic: On his return Yi told Gui:

sentences.zh: 「燕主衰老，太子闇弱，范陽王自負材氣；

translations.literal: "The Yan ruler is aged; the crown prince is dim and weak; the Prince of Fanyang trusts in his own talent and spirit;
translations.idiomatic: "The Yan ruler is old; the crown prince is dull and weak; Prince Murong De of Fanyang is proud of his ability;

sentences.zh: 非少主臣也。

translations.literal: they will not long serve a young lord.
translations.idiomatic: they will not serve a young master for long.

sentences.zh: 燕主既沒，內難必作，於明乃可圖也，今則未可。」

translations.literal: After the Yan ruler dies, inner strife is sure to arise—then one may plan against them; not yet."
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yan ruler is gone, civil strife will surely break out—then we can move against them; not yet."

sentences.zh: 珪善之。

translations.literal: Gui approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Gui thought well of this advice.

sentences.zh: 儀，珪母弟翰之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Han, younger brother of Gui's mother.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the son of Han, Tuoba Gui's uncle on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 九月，河南王乾歸遷都金城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Prince of Henan, Qian'gui, moved the capital to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Prince Qifu Qian'gui of Henan moved his capital to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 張申攻廣平，王祖攻樂陵；

translations.literal: Zhang Shen attacked Guangping; Wang Zu attacked Leling;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shen attacked Guangping and Wang Zu attacked Leling;

sentences.zh: 壬午，燕高陽王隆將兵討之。

translations.literal: On renwu, the Prince of Gaoyang, Long, led troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Prince Murong Long of Gaoyang marched against them.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，後秦主萇還安定。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Later Qin ruler Chang returned to Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Later Qin ruler Yao Chang returned to Anding.

sentences.zh: 秦主登就食新平，帥眾萬餘圍萇營，四面大哭；

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng foraged at Xinping and led more than ten thousand men to surround Chang's camp, wailing on all four sides;
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin ruler Fu Deng foraged at Xinping and led more than ten thousand men to surround Yao Chang's camp, wailing on all four sides;

sentences.zh: 萇命營中哭以應之，登乃退。

translations.literal: Chang ordered the camp to wail in reply, and Deng withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ordered his camp to wail back, and Deng pulled away.

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚子，尚書令南康襄公謝石卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Xie Shi, Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke Xiang of Nankang, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengzi, Xie Shi, Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke Xiang of Nankang, died.

sentences.zh: 燕太原王楷、趙王麟將兵會高陽王隆於合口，以擊張申；

translations.literal: The Yan Prince of Taiyuan, Kai, and the Prince of Zhao, Lin, led troops to join the Prince of Gaoyang, Long, at Hekou to attack Zhang Shen;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Kai of Taiyuan and Prince Murong Lin of Zhao led troops to join Prince Murong Long of Gaoyang at Hekou and attack Zhang Shen;

sentences.zh: 王祖帥諸壘共救之，夜犯燕軍，燕人逆擊走之。

translations.literal: Wang Zu led all the forts jointly to rescue Shen, attacked the Yan army by night, and the Yan forces met them and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zu led every nearby fort to the rescue, struck the Yan army by night, and the Yan troops met them and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 隆欲追之，楷、麟曰：「王祖老賊，或詐走而設伏，不如俟明。」

translations.literal: Long wished to pursue; Kai and Lin said, "Wang Zu is an old bandit—he may feign flight and lay an ambush. Better wait until daylight."
translations.idiomatic: Long wanted to pursue; Kai and Lin said, "Wang Zu is an old fox—he may be faking retreat to set an ambush. Better wait for dawn."

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「此白地群盜，烏合而來，徼幸一決，非素有約束，能壹其進退也。

translations.literal: Long said, "These are open-country bandits gathered in a mob, gambling on one throw. They are not men of long-standing discipline who can advance and retreat as one.
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "These are plain-field bandits cobbled together for one lucky throw. They aren't a disciplined force that can move as one.

sentences.zh: 今失利而去，眾莫為用；

translations.literal: Now that they have lost and fled, none will follow them;
translations.idiomatic: Now that they've lost and run, no one will obey them;

sentences.zh: 乘勢追之，不過數里，可盡禽也。

translations.literal: press the pursuit and within a few li we can capture them all.
translations.idiomatic: press the chase and within a few li we can take them all.

sentences.zh: 申之所恃，惟在於祖，祖破，則申降矣。」

translations.literal: All Shen relies on is Zu; break Zu and Shen will surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Shen's only support is Zu; break Zu and Shen will yield."

sentences.zh: 乃留楷、麟守申壘，隆與平幼分道擊之，比明，大獲而還，懸所獲之首以示申。

translations.literal: He left Kai and Lin to hold Shen's fort while Long and Ping You split forces to strike; by daylight they returned with a great haul and hung the captured heads to show Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He left Kai and Lin to hold Shen's fort while Long and Ping You split up to attack; by dawn they returned in triumph and hung the heads they had taken for Shen to see.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，申出降，祖亦歸罪。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Shen came out and surrendered; Zu also submitted to judgment.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin Shen came out and surrendered; Zu submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 秦以穎川王同成為太尉。

translations.literal: Qin made the Prince of Yingchuan, Tongcheng, Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin made Prince Fu Tongcheng of Yingchuan Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 列宗孝武皇帝中之下太元十四年（

translations.literal: Middle and lower portion of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the fourteenth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: From the middle and latter part of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the fourteenth year of the Taiyuan era (

sentences.zh: 己丑，公元三八九年）

translations.literal: jichou, corresponding to the year 389 CE).
translations.idiomatic: jichou, corresponding to 389 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕以陽平王柔鎮襄國。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Yan posted the Prince of Yangping, Rou, at Xiangguo.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Yan posted Prince Murong Rou of Yangping at Xiangguo.

sentences.zh: 遼西王農在龍城五年，庶務修舉，乃上表曰：「臣頃因征即鎮，所統將士安逸積年，青、徐、荊、雍遺寇尚繁，願時代還，展竭微效，生無餘力，沒無遺恨，臣之志也。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Liaoxi, Nong, had been at Longcheng five years; routine affairs were well ordered. He submitted a memorial: "Your servant lately took command on campaign and has since held the frontier; the troops under me have rested for years. Bandits still plague Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yong—I wish to rotate back in due season and spend what strength remains, living without surplus force and dying without regret; such is your servant's wish."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Nong of Liaoxi had governed Longcheng for five years and kept affairs in good order. He memorialized the throne: "Your servant took this post on campaign and has held the frontier while my troops rested for years. Raiders still trouble Qing, Xu, Jing, and Yong—I ask to rotate home in turn, spend what strength I have left, live without reserve, and die without regret. That is my wish."

sentences.zh: 庚申，燕主垂召農為侍中、司隸校尉。

translations.literal: On gengshen the Yan ruler Chui summoned Nong as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Colonel-Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Murong Chui recalled Nong as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Colonel-Director of Retainers.

sentences.zh: 以高陽王隆為都督幽、平二州諸軍事、征北大將軍、幽州牧，建留台於龍城，以隆錄留台尚書事。

translations.literal: He made the Prince of Gaoyang, Long, Commander of all military affairs in You and Ping, Grand General Who Conquers the North, and Governor of You; established a rear headquarters at Longcheng and put Long in charge as Director of the Masters of Writing for the rear headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He made Prince Murong Long of Gaoyang commander of You and Ping, Grand General Who Conquers the North, and Governor of You; set up a rear headquarters at Longcheng and put Long in charge of its Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 又以護軍將軍平幼為征北長史，散騎常侍封孚為司馬，並兼留台尚書。

translations.literal: He also made Protector-General Ping You Chief Clerk of the Northern Expedition, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Feng Fu Major, both additionally Masters of Writing for the rear headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Protector-General Ping You chief clerk of the northern expedition, Regular Attendant Feng Fu major, both additionally Masters of Writing at the rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 隆因農舊規，修而廣之，遼、碣由是遂安。

translations.literal: Long built upon Nong's former regulations, repairing and enlarging them; Liaodong and Jieshi were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Long took Nong's old rules, repaired and expanded them, and Liaodong and Jieshi were thereby settled.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇以秦戰屢勝，謂得秦王堅之神助，亦於軍中立堅像而禱之曰：「臣史襄敕臣復仇，新平之禍，臣行襄之命，非臣罪也。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang, since Qin forces had won repeatedly in battle, believed he had the divine aid of King Fu Jian of Qin. He too erected an image of Jian in camp and prayed: "Your servant was commanded by Shi Xiang to take revenge. The calamity at Xinping—I carried out Xiang's order, not your servant's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang, seeing Former Qin win battle after battle, believed he had the divine aid of King Fu Jian of Former Qin. He too set up an image of Jian in camp and prayed: "Shi Xiang ordered me to take revenge. The disaster at Xinping—I carried out Xiang's command, not my own crime.

sentences.zh: 苻登，陛下疏屬，猶欲復仇，況臣敢忘其兄乎？

translations.literal: Fu Deng, Your Majesty's distant kinsman, still seeks revenge—how much less could your servant forget his elder brother?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng, Your Majesty's distant kinsman, still seeks revenge—how could I forget my own elder brother?

sentences.zh: 且陛下命臣以龍驤建業，臣敢違之？

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty charged your servant with the Dragon Soaring command to build the enterprise—how could your servant defy it?
translations.idiomatic: And Your Majesty charged me with the Dragon-Soaring command to build the realm—how could I refuse?

sentences.zh: 今為陛下立像，陛下勿追計臣過也。」

translations.literal: I now erect this image for Your Majesty; may Your Majesty not hold your servant's transgressions against me."
translations.idiomatic: I set up this image for Your Majesty now; pray do not hold my faults against me."

sentences.zh: 秦主登升樓，遙謂萇曰：「為臣弒君，而立像求福，庸有益乎？」

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng climbed a tower and shouted across to Chang: "To murder your lord as a subject, then set up an image seeking blessing—can that do any good?"
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin ruler Fu Deng climbed a tower and shouted across to Chang: "You murdered your sovereign as a subject, then set up an image to beg for blessing—what good can that do?"

sentences.zh: 因大呼曰：「弒君賊姚萇何不自出？

translations.literal: He then cried out: "Murderer of his sovereign Yao Chang—why do you not come out yourself?
translations.idiomatic: Then he cried, "Regicide Yao Chang—why don't you come out yourself?

sentences.zh: 吾與汝決之！」

translations.literal: I will settle it with you!"
translations.idiomatic: I'll settle this with you!"

sentences.zh: 萇不應。

translations.literal: Chang did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Chang made no reply.

sentences.zh: 久之，以戰未有利，軍中每夜數驚，乃斬像首以送秦。

translations.literal: After some time, since battle had brought no advantage and the camp panicked nightly, he cut off the image's head and sent it to Qin.
translations.idiomatic: After a while, with no victory in sight and the camp shaken by nightly alarms, he cut off the image's head and sent it to Former Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦主登以河南王乾歸為大將軍、大單于、金城王。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng made the Prince of Henan, Qian'gui, Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin ruler Fu Deng made Prince Qifu Qian'gui of Henan Grand General, Grand Chanyu, and Prince of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，魏王珪襲高車，破之。

translations.literal: On jiayin the Wei king, Tuoba Gui, raided the Gaoche and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin King Tuoba Gui of Wei raided the Gaoche and routed them.

sentences.zh: 二月，品光自稱三河王，大赦，改元麟嘉，置百官。

translations.literal: In the second month, Lü Guang declared himself Prince of Three Rivers, proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name to Linjia, and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lü Guang declared himself Prince of Three Rivers, proclaimed a general amnesty, adopted the era name Linjia, and set up a full bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 光妻石氏、子紹、弟德世自仇池來至姑臧，光立石氏為妃，紹為世子。

translations.literal: Guang's wife Lady Shi, his son Shao, and his brother Deshi came from Chouci to Guzang; Guang installed Lady Shi as consort and Shao as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's wife Lady Shi, his son Shao, and his brother Deshi came from Chouci to Guzang; he made Lady Shi consort and Shao heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，魏王珪擊吐突鄰部於女水，大破之，盡徙其部落而還。

translations.literal: On guisi the Wei king, Tuoba Gui, attacked the Tutu Lin tribe at the Nu River, routed them utterly, relocated the entire tribe, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi King Tuoba Gui of Wei attacked the Tutu Lin tribe at the Nu River, crushed them, moved the whole tribe, and returned.

sentences.zh: 秦主登留輜重於大界，自將輕騎萬餘攻安定羌密造保，克之。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng left his baggage train at Dajie and personally led more than ten thousand light horse to attack the Qiang fortified camp of Mizao in Anding and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin ruler Fu Deng left his baggage at Dajie and personally led more than ten thousand light cavalry to attack the Qiang stronghold of Mizao in Anding and took it.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，翟遼寇滎陽，執太守張卓。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Zhai Liao raided Xingyang and seized Administrator Zhang Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Zhai Liao raided Xingyang and captured Administrator Zhang Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 燕以長樂公盛鎮薊城，修繕舊宮。

translations.literal: Yan posted Duke Sheng of Changle at Jicheng, repairing the old palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yan posted Duke Murong Sheng of Changle at Jicheng and restored the old palace.

sentences.zh: 五月，清河民孔金斬吳深，送首中山。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Kong Jin of Qinghe beheaded Wu Shen and sent the head to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Kong Jin of Qinghe beheaded Wu Shen and sent his head to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 金城王乾歸擊侯年部，大破之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jincheng, Qian'gui, attacked the tribal forces of Hounian and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qifu Qian'gui of Jincheng attacked the Hounian tribe and routed them.

sentences.zh: 於是秦、涼、鮮卑、羌、胡多附乾歸，乾歸悉授以官爵。

translations.literal: Thereupon many from Qin, Liang, Xianbei, Qiang, and Hu submitted to Qian'gui, and he invested them all with offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter many leaders from Qin, Liang, the Xianbei, Qiang, and other tribes submitted to Qian'gui, and he invested them all with offices and titles.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇與秦主登戰，數敗，乃遣中軍將軍姚崇襲大界。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang fought the Qin ruler Deng, was repeatedly defeated, and sent Central Army General Yao Chong to raid Dajie.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang fought Former Qin ruler Fu Deng, lost again and again, and sent Central Army General Yao Chong to raid Dajie.

sentences.zh: 登邀擊之於安丘，又敗之。

translations.literal: Deng intercepted him at Anqiu and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: Deng intercepted him at Anqiu and beat him again.

sentences.zh: 燕范陽王德、趙王麟擊賀訥，追奔至勿根山，訥窮迫請降，徙上之上谷，質其弟染干於中山。

translations.literal: The Yan Prince of Fanyang, De, and the Prince of Zhao, Lin, attacked He Na, pursued the rout to Wugen Mountain; Na, cornered, begged to surrender. His tribe was moved to Shanggu, and his younger brother Ran'gan was kept as hostage at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong De of Fanyang and Prince Murong Lin of Zhao attacked He Na and chased the rout to Wugen Mountain; cornered, Na begged to surrender. His tribe was relocated to Shanggu, and his younger brother Ran'gan was held hostage at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以驃騎長史王忱為荊州刺史、都督荊、益、寧三州諸軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Chen was made Inspector of Jingzhou and Commander of all military affairs in Jing, Yi, and Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wang Chen was made Inspector of Jing and commander of Jing, Yi, and Ning.

sentences.zh: 忱，國寶之弟也。

translations.literal: Chen was the younger brother of Wang Guobao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was the younger brother of Wang Guobao.

sentences.zh: 秦主登攻後秦右將軍吳忠等於平涼，克之。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng attacked Later Qin Right General Wu Zhong and others at Pingliang and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin ruler Fu Deng attacked Later Qin Right General Wu Zhong and others at Pingliang and took it.

sentences.zh: 八月，登據苟頭原以逼安定。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Deng occupied Gutou Plain to press Anding.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Deng seized Gutou Plain to press Anding.

sentences.zh: 諸將勸後秦主萇決戰，萇曰：「與窮寇競勝，兵家之忌也，吾將以計取之。」

translations.literal: The generals urged the Later Qin ruler Chang to fight a decisive battle; Chang said, "To vie for victory with cornered foes is what strategists forbid—I will take them by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged Later Qin ruler Yao Chang to fight a decisive battle; Chang said, "Fighting cornered enemies for a quick win is what strategists warn against—I will take them by stratagem."

sentences.zh: 乃留尚書令姚旻守安定，夜，帥騎三萬襲秦輜重於大界，克之，殺毛后及南安王弁、北海王尚，擒名將數十人，驅掠男女五萬餘口而還。
