translations.literal: He left Director of the Masters of Writing Yao Min to hold Anding; by night he led thirty thousand horse to raid Qin's baggage at Dajie, took it, killed Empress Mao and Prince Bian of Nan'an and Prince Shang of Beihai, captured several dozen famed generals, and drove off more than fifty thousand men and women before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He left Director Yao Min to hold Anding; by night he led thirty thousand cavalry to raid Former Qin's baggage train at Dajie, took it, killed Empress Mao and Princes Fu Bian of Nan'an and Fu Shang of Beihai, captured dozens of noted generals, and drove off more than fifty thousand captives before returning.

sentences.zh: 毛氏美而勇，善騎射。

translations.literal: Lady Mao was beautiful and brave, skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Mao was beautiful and fierce, skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 後秦兵入其營，毛氏猶彎弓跨馬，帥壯士數百力戰，殺七百餘人。

translations.literal: When Later Qin troops entered her camp, Lady Mao still strung her bow and mounted her horse, leading several hundred stalwarts to fight tenaciously and kill more than seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Qin troops broke into her camp, Lady Mao still strung her bow, mounted her horse, and led several hundred warriors in a fierce fight, killing more than seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 眾寡不敵，為後秦所執。

translations.literal: Outnumbered, she was seized by Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, she was captured by Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 萇將納之，毛氏罵且哭曰：「姚萇，汝先已殺天子，今又欲辱皇后。

translations.literal: Chang meant to take her as consort; Lady Mao cursed and wept: "Yao Chang—you already killed the Son of Heaven, and now you would dishonor the empress?
translations.idiomatic: Chang meant to take her as consort; Lady Mao cursed and wept: "Yao Chang—you already killed the Son of Heaven, and now you would dishonor the empress?

sentences.zh: 皇天后土，寧汝容乎？」

translations.literal: Would Heaven and Earth bear you?"
translations.idiomatic: Would Heaven and Earth tolerate you?"

sentences.zh: 萇殺之。

translations.literal: Chang killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had her killed.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲因秦軍駭亂擊之，萇曰：「登眾雖亂，怒氣猶盛，未可輕也。」

translations.literal: The generals wished to strike while Qin's army was in disorder; Chang said, "Though Deng's host is disarrayed, their rage is still strong—not to be treated lightly."
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted to strike while Former Qin's army was in chaos; Chang said, "Deng's troops may be disordered, but their fury is still fierce—not to be taken lightly."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: He desisted.
translations.idiomatic: He held them back.

sentences.zh: 登收餘眾屯胡空堡。

translations.literal: Deng gathered the remnant forces and encamped at Hukong Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Deng gathered his remnants and encamped at Hukong Fortress.

sentences.zh: 萇使姚碩德鎮安定，徙安定千餘家於陰密，遣其弟征南將軍靖鎮之。

translations.literal: Chang posted Yao Shuode at Anding, moved more than a thousand households from Anding to Yinmi, and sent his younger brother Southern Expedition General Yao Jing to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Chang posted Yao Shuode at Anding, moved more than a thousand Anding households to Yinmi, and sent his younger brother Southern Expedition General Yao Jing to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚午，以左僕射陸納為尚書令。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengwu, Lu Na, Left Vice Director, was made Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengwu, Left Vice Director Lu Na was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 秦主登之東也，後秦主萇使姚碩德置秦州守宰，以從弟常戍隴城，邢奴戍冀城，姚詳戍略陽。

translations.literal: When the Qin ruler Deng marched east, the Later Qin ruler Chang had Yao Shuode appoint guards and magistrates for Qinzhou, posting his younger cousin Chang at Longcheng, Xingnu at Jicheng, and Yao Xiang at Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Former Qin ruler Fu Deng marched east, Later Qin ruler Yao Chang had Yao Shuode appoint Qinzhou garrisons and magistrates, posting his cousin Yao Chang at Longcheng, Xingnu at Jicheng, and Yao Xiang at Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 楊定攻隴、冀，克之，斬常，執邢奴，詳棄略陽，奔陰密。

translations.literal: Yang Ding attacked Long and Ji, took them, killed Chang, captured Xingnu; Xiang abandoned Lueyang and fled to Yinmi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ding attacked Longcheng and Jicheng, took them, killed Yao Chang, captured Xingnu; Yao Xiang abandoned Lueyang and fled to Yinmi.

sentences.zh: 定自稱秦州牧、隴西王，秦因其所稱而授之。

translations.literal: Ding declared himself Governor of Qinzhou and Prince of Longxi; Qin confirmed the titles he had taken for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ding declared himself Governor of Qin and Prince of Longxi; Former Qin ratified the titles he had assumed.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，秦主登以竇沖為大司馬、都督隴東諸軍事、雍州牧，楊定為左丞相、都督中外諸軍事、秦、梁二州牧，楊壁為都督隴右諸軍事，南秦、益二州牧，約與共攻後秦；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, the Qin ruler Deng made Dou Chong Grand Commandant, Commander of all military affairs east of Long, and Governor of Yong; Yang Ding Left Chancellor, Commander of all military affairs within and without, and Governor of Qin and Liang; Yang Bi Commander of all military affairs west of Long, and Governor of Southern Qin and Yi; and arranged jointly to attack Later Qin;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Former Qin ruler Fu Deng made Dou Chong Grand Commandant, commander of the armies east of Long, and Governor of Yong; Yang Ding Left Chancellor, commander of all armies at home and abroad, and Governor of Qin and Liang; Yang Bi commander of the armies west of Long and Governor of Southern Qin and Yi; and pledged with them to attack Later Qin together;

sentences.zh: 又約監河西諸軍事、并州刺史楊政、都督河東諸軍事、冀州刺史楊楷各其眾會長安。

translations.literal: He also summoned Yang Zheng, Inspector-Director of military affairs west of the river and Governor of Bing, and Yang Kai, Commander of military affairs east of the river and Inspector of Ji, each with his forces to assemble at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He also called on Yang Zheng, overseer of military affairs west of the river and Governor of Bing, and Yang Kai, commander of military affairs east of the river and Inspector of Ji, each to bring his forces to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 政、楷皆河東人。

translations.literal: Zheng and Kai were both natives of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Kai were both men of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 秦主丕既敗，政、楷收集流民數萬戶，政據河西，楷據湖、陝之間，遣使請命於秦，登因而授之。

translations.literal: After the Qin ruler Pi was defeated, Zheng and Kai gathered several tens of thousands of refugee households; Zheng held the land west of the river, Kai held the region between Hu and Shan, sent envoys to request orders from Qin, and Deng invested them accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: After Former Qin ruler Fu Pi was defeated, Zheng and Kai gathered tens of thousands of refugee households; Zheng held the west of the river, Kai held the ground between Hu and Shan. They sent envoys to seek appointment from Former Qin, and Deng invested them.

sentences.zh: 燕樂浪悼王溫為冀州刺史，翟遼遣丁零故堤詐降於溫，為溫帳下，乙酉，刺溫，殺之，並其長史司馬驅，帥守兵二百戶奔西燕。

translations.literal: The Yan Prince of Lelang, Wen, was Inspector of Ji; Zhai Liao sent the Dingling defector Gudi to feign surrender to Wen and serve in Wen's retinue. On yiyou he stabbed Wen, killed him, and also killed his chief clerk Sima Qu; then led two hundred garrison households to flee to Western Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Wen of Lelang was Inspector of Ji; Zhai Liao sent the Dingling turncoat Gudi to feign surrender and serve in Wen's retinue. On yiyou Gudi stabbed Wen, killed him, and killed his chief clerk Sima Qu as well; then led two hundred garrison households in flight to Western Yan.

sentences.zh: 遼西王農邀擊於襄國，盡獲之，惟堤走免。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liaoxi, Nong, intercepted them at Xiangguo and captured them all; only Gudi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Nong of Liaoxi intercepted them at Xiangguo and captured them all; only Gudi got away.

sentences.zh: 十一月，枹罕羌彭奚念附於乞伏乾歸，以奚念為北河州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Qiang Peng Xinian of Fuhan submitted to Qifu Qian'gui, who made Xinian Governor of Northern Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Fuhan Qiang leader Peng Xinian submitted to Qifu Qian'gui, who made him Governor of Northern He.

sentences.zh: 初，帝既親政事，威權己出，有人主之量。

translations.literal: At first, once the emperor personally handled state affairs, authority had left the throne and he had the measure of a true ruler.
translations.idiomatic: At first, once the emperor took government into his own hands, power rested with him and he showed the makings of a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 已而溺於酒色，委事於琅邪王道子。

translations.literal: Before long he drowned in wine and women and entrusted affairs to Prince Daozi of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he drowned in wine and women and handed affairs over to Prince Sima Daozi of Langya.

sentences.zh: 道子亦嗜酒，日夕與帝以酣歌為事。

translations.literal: Daozi also loved wine and spent day and night with the emperor in drunken song.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi also loved wine and spent day and night with the emperor in drunken revelry.

sentences.zh: 又崇尚浮屠，窮奢極費，所親暱者皆□甘姆、僧尼。

translations.literal: They also revered Buddhism, exhausted the treasury on luxury, and those they favored and kept near were courtesans, wet nurses, and Buddhist monks and nuns.
translations.idiomatic: They also embraced Buddhism, spent extravagantly, and those they kept close were courtesans, wet nurses, and Buddhist monks and nuns.

sentences.zh: 左右近習，爭弄權柄，交通請托，賄賂公行，官賞濫雜，刑獄謬亂。

translations.literal: Those close at hand on left and right vied to wield power, traded in requests and patronage, bribery went on openly, official rewards and punishments were recklessly mixed, and criminal justice was absurdly confused.
translations.idiomatic: Those around the throne vied for power, traded favors and patronage, bribery ran rampant, offices and punishments were handed out without restraint, and the courts were in chaos.

sentences.zh: 尚書令陸納望宮闕歎曰：「好家居，纖兒欲撞壞之邪？」

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Na looked toward the palace gates and sighed, saying, "What a fine household — does this weakling mean to smash it to pieces?"
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Na gazed at the palace gates and sighed, "What a fine house — and this weakling means to wreck it?"

sentences.zh: 左衛領營將軍會稽許營上疏曰：「今台府局吏、直衛武官及僕隸婢兒取母之姓者，本無鄉邑品第，皆得為郡守縣令，或帶職在內，及僧尼乳母，競進親黨，又受貨賂；

translations.literal: Left Guard Commanding Camp General Xu Ying of Kuaiji submitted a memorial saying, "Today bureau clerks of the central administration, direct-guard military officers, and servants and slave-girls who take their mother's surname — who originally had no native-place rank or pedigree — all become prefects and magistrates, or hold office within the palace; Buddhist monks, nuns, and wet nurses all push forward their kin, and also accept bribes;
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard Commanding Camp General Xu Ying of Kuaiji submitted a memorial: "Today central-administration clerks, palace-guard officers, and servants and slave-girls who bear their mothers' surnames — men with no pedigree or native rank — are made prefects and magistrates, or hold posts inside the palace. Monks, nuns, and wet nurses all push forward their relatives and take bribes as well;

sentences.zh: 輒臨官領眾，政教不均，暴濫無罪，禁令不明，劫盜公行。

translations.literal: They then take office and command troops; government and instruction are uneven, the innocent are abused without cause, prohibitions are unclear, and robbery and banditry go on openly.
translations.idiomatic: They take office and command troops, yet govern unevenly, abuse the innocent, enforce no clear law, and leave robbery and banditry to flourish in the open.

sentences.zh: 昔年下書敕群下盡規，而眾議兼集，無所採用。

translations.literal: In years past edicts were issued ordering all officials to offer remonstrance, yet though many opinions were gathered together, none were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: In years past the throne ordered all officials to speak freely, yet though advice poured in from every side, none of it was heeded.

sentences.zh: 臣聞佛者清遠玄虛之神，今僧尼往往依傍法服，五誡粗法尚不能遵，況精妙乎？

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the Buddha is a spirit pure, remote, and abstruse; yet today monks and nuns often rely on monastic robes while they cannot even observe the five precepts and the rough rudiments of the Law — how much less its subtle refinements?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the Buddha is a spirit of purity and distant mystery, yet monks and nuns today wear the robes while failing even to keep the five precepts and the most basic rules — to say nothing of the deeper teaching.

sentences.zh: 而流惑之徒，競加敬事，又侵漁百姓，取材為惠，亦未合佈施之道也。」

translations.literal: Yet the deluded masses compete to honor and serve them; they also prey on the common people and take from others to dispense as favors — this too does not accord with the way of charity."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the deluded public vies to honor them, while they prey on the people and take from others to give as favors — a practice that falls far short of true charity."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 道子勢傾內外，遠近奔湊。

translations.literal: Daozi's power tilted inward and outward, and men near and far rushed to gather around him.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi's power overshadowed court and realm alike, and men from near and far flocked to his side.

sentences.zh: 帝漸不平，然猶外加優崇。

translations.literal: The emperor gradually grew resentful, yet outwardly he still treated Daozi with exceptional honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew increasingly uneasy, yet still treated Daozi with outward favor and high honor.

sentences.zh: 侍中王國寶以讒佞有寵於道子，扇動朝眾，諷八座啟道子宜進位丞相、揚州牧，假黃鉞，加殊禮。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Wang Guobao, slanderous and fawning, was favored by Daozi; he stirred the court assembly and prompted the Eight Ministers to memorialize that Daozi should be advanced to Chancellor, Governor of Yangzhou, granted the yellow battle-axe, and given extraordinary honors.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wang Guobao, a slanderer and flatterer favored by Daozi, stirred the court and prompted the Eight Ministers to recommend that Daozi be made Chancellor and Governor of Yangzhou, granted the yellow battle-axe, and accorded extraordinary honors.

sentences.zh: 護軍將軍南平車胤曰：「此乃成王所以尊周公也。

translations.literal: Protector-General Che Yin of Nanping said, "This is how King Cheng of Zhou honored the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Che Yin of Nanping said, "That was how King Cheng honored the Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今主上當陽，非成王之比。

translations.literal: Today our sovereign sits facing the sun; he is no match for King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign today sits firmly on the throne — he is no child-king like Cheng.

sentences.zh: 相王在位，豈得為周公乎？」

translations.literal: The Prince Regent holds office — how can he be the Duke of Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince Regent already holds power — how can he be treated as another Duke of Zhou?"

sentences.zh: 乃稱疾不署。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness and refused to sign.
translations.idiomatic: He then pleaded illness and refused to sign the memorial.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝大怒，而嘉胤有守。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was greatly angered, yet he admired Yin for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor flew into a rage — yet he admired Yin for standing firm.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎范寧、徐邈為帝所親信，數進忠言，補正闕失，指斥奸黨。

translations.literal: Secretary of the Masters of Writing Fan Ning and Xu Miao were trusted by the emperor; they repeatedly offered loyal counsel, corrected omissions and errors, and denounced the faction of villains.
translations.idiomatic: Secretaries Fan Ning and Xu Miao enjoyed the emperor's trust; they repeatedly offered loyal counsel, corrected government failings, and denounced the corrupt faction.

sentences.zh: 王國寶，寧之甥也。

translations.literal: Wang Guobao was Ning's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao was Fan Ning's nephew.

sentences.zh: 寧尤疾其阿諛，勸帝黜之。

translations.literal: Ning especially hated his flattery and urged the emperor to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Ning especially despised his flattery and urged the emperor to remove him from office.

sentences.zh: 陳郡袁悅之有寵於道子，國寶使悅之因尼克妙音致書於太子母陳淑媛云：「國寶忠謹，宜見親信。」

translations.literal: Yuan Yuezhi of Chen Commandery was favored by Daozi; Guobao had Yuezhi go through Nun Zhi Miaoyin to deliver a letter to the crown prince's mother, Lady Chen Shu, saying, "Guobao is loyal and careful and ought to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yuezhi of Chen Commandery was a favorite of Daozi; Guobao had Yuezhi send a letter through Nun Zhi Miaoyin to the crown prince's mother, Lady Chen Shu, saying, "Guobao is loyal and conscientious and deserves the emperor's trust."

sentences.zh: 帝知之，發怒，托以他事斬悅之。

translations.literal: When the emperor learned of it, he grew angry and, using another matter as pretext, had Yuezhi executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of it, he was furious and had Yuezhi executed on a pretext.

sentences.zh: 國寶大懼，與道子共譖范寧出為豫章太守。

translations.literal: Guobao was greatly afraid; together with Daozi he slandered Fan Ning until the emperor sent him out as Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao was terrified; he and Daozi joined in slandering Fan Ning until the emperor posted him as Administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 寧臨發，上疏言：「今邊烽不舉而倉庫空匱。

translations.literal: As Ning was about to depart, he submitted a memorial saying, "Today the frontier beacons are not raised, yet the storehouses stand empty.
translations.idiomatic: As Ning prepared to leave, he submitted a memorial: "The frontier is quiet, yet the storehouses stand empty.

sentences.zh: 古者使民歲不過三日，今之勞擾，殆無三日之休。

translations.literal: In antiquity the people were levied for labor no more than three days a year; today their toil and exactions leave them scarcely three days of rest.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity corvée labor took no more than three days a year; today the people are worked and harassed until they scarcely know three days' rest.

sentences.zh: 至有生兒不復舉養，鰥寡不敢嫁娶。

translations.literal: It has reached the point that some bear children and then do not raise them, and widowers and widows dare not marry.
translations.idiomatic: Some now bear children they will not raise, and widows and widowers dare not remarry.

sentences.zh: 臣恐社稷之憂，厝火積薪，不足喻也。」

translations.literal: Your servant fears the state's peril cannot even be likened to fire laid upon piled kindling."
translations.idiomatic: I fear the peril to the state is worse than fire heaped on kindling — and even that image falls short."

sentences.zh: 寧又上言：「中原士民流寓江左，歲月漸久，人安其業。

translations.literal: Ning also submitted another memorial: "The gentry and common people of the Central Plains who fled and settled south of the Yangzi have grown accustomed over the years and are secure in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Ning submitted another memorial: "The gentry and common people of the Central Plains who fled south of the Yangzi have lived there for years and settled into their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 凡天下之人，原其先祖，皆隨世適移，何至於今而獨不可？

translations.literal: All people under Heaven, tracing their ancestors back, have moved with the age and settled where they went — why should today alone be impossible?
translations.idiomatic: Tracing any family's ancestors, all people have moved with the times and settled where they went — why should our age alone be the exception?

sentences.zh: 謂宜正其封疆，戶口皆以土斷。

translations.literal: Your servant holds that their territories ought to be fixed and household registers all subject to land registration by actual residence.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that their jurisdictions should be fixed and all households registered according to where they actually live.

sentences.zh: 又，人性無涯，奢儉由勢；

translations.literal: Moreover, human desire knows no bound; extravagance or thrift follows circumstance;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, human wants know no limit; whether people live lavishly or frugally depends on the example set around them;

sentences.zh: 今並廉之室，亦多不贍，非其財力不足，蓋由用之無節，爭以靡麗相高，無有亦限極故也。

translations.literal: today even households famed for integrity often cannot make ends meet — not because their wealth is insufficient, but because spending knows no restraint, all compete to outdo one another in splendor, and there is no limit or end to it.
translations.idiomatic: today even households known for integrity often cannot make ends meet — not from lack of means, but because spending has no restraint, everyone vies in luxury, and there is no limit to the competition.

sentences.zh: 禮十九為長殤，以其未成人也。

translations.literal: According to ritual, nineteen counts as a long untimely death, because the person has not yet reached adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual treats nineteen as a long untimely death, because the person is not yet fully grown.

sentences.zh: 今以十六為全丁，十三為半丁，所任非復童幼之事，豈不傷天理、困百姓乎？

translations.literal: Today sixteen counts as a full laborer and thirteen as a half laborer, and the tasks assigned are no longer those fit for children — does this not wound Heaven's principle and burden the people?
translations.idiomatic: Today sixteen counts as a full laborer and thirteen as a half laborer, and the duties assigned are no longer fit for children — does this not violate natural justice and crush the people?

sentences.zh: 謂宜以二十為全丁，十六為半丁，則人無夭折，生長繁滋矣。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds that twenty ought to count as a full laborer and sixteen as a half laborer; then men would not die young and the population would grow and flourish."
translations.idiomatic: I hold that twenty should count as a full laborer and sixteen as a half laborer; then fewer would die young and the population would grow and flourish."

sentences.zh: 帝多納用之。

translations.literal: The emperor largely accepted and adopted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely accepted and adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 寧在豫章，遣十五議曹下屬城，采求風政，並吏假還，訊問官長得失。

translations.literal: While Ning was at Yuzhang, he sent fifteen review clerks down to the subordinate districts to gather reports on local customs and governance, and also had clerks on leave return home to inquire into the merits and faults of local officials.
translations.idiomatic: While Ning was at Yuzhang, he sent fifteen review clerks into the subordinate districts to investigate local customs and governance, and also had clerks on leave return home to inquire into the conduct of local officials.

sentences.zh: 徐邈與寧書曰：「足下聽斷有允，庶事無滯，則吏慎其負，而人聽不惑矣，豈須邑至裡詣，飾其游聲哉！

translations.literal: Xu Miao wrote to Ning, saying, "If you, sir, decide cases fairly and all affairs proceed without delay, then officials will be careful in their duties and the people will not be confused in their hearing — why must you go from district to village and hamlet to hamlet, polishing your traveling reputation!
translations.idiomatic: Xu Miao wrote to Ning: "If you decide cases fairly and keep affairs moving, officials will do their duty and the people will not be misled — why must you go from district to village polishing your reputation as you travel!

sentences.zh: 非徒不足致益，乃實蠶漁之所資，豈有善人群子而干非其事，多所告白者乎！

translations.literal: Far from bringing any benefit, this is in truth fodder for petty extortion — would a good and upright gentleman meddle in what is not his business and lodge many accusations?
translations.idiomatic: Far from doing any good, it only feeds petty extortion — would a good and upright man meddle in what is not his business and encourage a flood of accusations?

sentences.zh: 自古以來，欲為左右耳目者，無非小人，皆先因小忠而成其大不忠，先藉小信而成其大不信，遂使讒謅並進，善惡倒置，可不戒哉？

translations.literal: From antiquity to the present, those who wish to be eyes and ears at one's side have without exception been petty men; all first use small loyalty to achieve great disloyalty, first borrow small trust to achieve great betrayal, and thus slander and flattery advance together while good and evil are reversed — can one not be on guard?
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity onward, those who wish to be a ruler's eyes and ears have always been petty men: they begin with small acts of loyalty to achieve great treachery, win small trust to betray it fully, and so slander and flattery advance together while good and evil are reversed — should one not be on guard?

sentences.zh: 足下慎選綱紀，必得國土以攝諸曹，諸曹皆得良吏以掌文按，又擇公方之人以為監司，則清濁能否，與事而明，足下但平心處之，何取於耳目哉？

translations.literal: If you, sir, carefully choose your chief officers, appoint men of true talent to oversee the bureaus, place good officials in every bureau to manage documents and cases, and select upright men as inspectors, then what is clear or murky and who is capable or not will become plain through the work itself; you need only handle matters with an even heart — what need is there for personal spies?
translations.idiomatic: Choose your chief officers carefully, put men of real talent in charge of the bureaus, place capable clerks in every office to handle documents and cases, and appoint upright men as inspectors — then merit and corruption, ability and incompetence, will become plain through the work itself. You need only judge with an even hand; what need is there for personal spies?

sentences.zh: 昔明德馬後未嘗顧左右與言，可謂遠識，況大丈夫而不能免此乎！」

translations.literal: In the past Empress Ma the Illustrious never turned to those at her side to speak with them — that may be called far-sighted wisdom; how much more, then, should a great man be able to avoid this trap!"
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ma the Illustrious never turned to those at her side for counsel — that was true foresight; surely a man of stature ought to be able to do the same!"

sentences.zh: 十二月，後秦主萇使其東門將軍任盆詐遣使招秦主登，許開門納之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Later Qin ruler Chang had his Eastern Gate General Ren Pen feign sending an envoy to recruit the Qin ruler Deng, promising to open the gates and admit him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Later Qin ruler Yao Chang had his Eastern Gate General Ren Pen send a feigned envoy to win over Former Qin ruler Fu Deng, promising to open the gates and admit him.

sentences.zh: 登將從之，征東將軍雷惡地將兵在外，聞之，馳騎見登，曰：「姚萇多許，不可信也！」

translations.literal: Deng was about to agree when Eastern Expedition General Lei E'di, commanding troops abroad, heard of it, galloped to see Deng, and said, "Yao Chang is full of deceit and cannot be trusted!"
translations.idiomatic: Deng was about to accept when Eastern Expedition General Lei E'di, campaigning abroad, heard of it, rode in haste to see Deng, and said, "Yao Chang is treacherous — he cannot be trusted!"

sentences.zh: 登乃止。

translations.literal: Deng then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Deng then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 萇聞惡地詣登，謂諸將曰：「此羌見登，事不成矣！」

translations.literal: When Chang heard that E'di had gone to Deng, he said to his generals, "That Qiang has seen Deng — the affair is ruined!"
translations.idiomatic: When Chang learned that E'di had gone to Deng, he told his generals, "That Qiang has seen Deng — the plan is ruined!"

sentences.zh: 登以惡地勇略過人，陰憚之。

translations.literal: Deng, because E'di's courage and strategy surpassed other men, secretly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Deng secretly feared E'di, whose courage and strategy surpassed other men.

sentences.zh: 惡地懼，降於後秦，萇以惡地為鎮軍將軍。

translations.literal: E'di, in fear, surrendered to Later Qin, and Chang made E'di Pacifying Army General.
translations.idiomatic: E'di, fearing for his life, surrendered to Later Qin, and Chang made him Pacifying Army General.

sentences.zh: 秦以安成王廣為司徒。

translations.literal: Qin made Prince Guang of Ancheng Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin made Prince Fu Guang of Ancheng Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 列宗孝武皇帝中之下太元十五年（

translations.literal: Annals of the House: middle and lower portion of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the fifteenth year of Taiyuan (
translations.idiomatic: From the middle and latter part of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the fifteenth year of the Taiyuan era (

sentences.zh: 庚寅，公元三九零年）

translations.literal: gengyin, corresponding to the year 390 CE).
translations.idiomatic: gengyin, corresponding to 390 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙亥，譙敬王恬薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Prince Tian the Respectful of Qiao died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yihai, Prince Sima Tian the Respectful of Qiao died.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永引兵向洛陽，朱序自河陰北濟河，擊敗之，永走還上黨。

translations.literal: The Western Yan ruler Yong led troops toward Luoyang; Zhu Xu crossed the Yellow River north from Heyin, defeated him, and Yong fled back to Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Western Yan ruler Murong Yong marched on Luoyang; Zhu Xu crossed the Yellow River north from Heyin, defeated him, and Yong fled back to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 序追至白水，會翟遼謀向洛陽，序乃引兵還，擊走之，留鷹揚將軍朱黨戍石門，使其子略督護洛陽，以參軍趙蕃佐之，身還襄陽。

translations.literal: Xu pursued as far as Baishui; when Zhai Liao plotted to march on Luoyang, Xu turned his army back, attacked and drove him off, left Hawk-Raising General Zhu Dang to garrison Shimen, had his son Lue oversee Luoyang with Staff Officer Zhao Fan to assist him, and returned in person to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu pursued as far as Baishui; when Zhai Liao plotted to march on Luoyang, Xu turned back, attacked and drove him off, left Hawk-Raising General Zhu Dang to garrison Shimen, put his son Zhu Lue in charge of Luoyang with Staff Officer Zhao Fan to assist him, and returned to Xiangyang himself.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王道子恃寵驕恣，侍宴酣醉，或虧禮敬。

translations.literal: Prince Daozi of Langya, relying on favor, grew arrogant and unrestrained; at banquets he drank to drunkenness and sometimes failed in ritual respect.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Daozi of Langya, secure in the emperor's favor, grew arrogant and unrestrained; at court banquets he drank himself drunk and sometimes showed disrespect.

sentences.zh: 帝浸不能平，欲選時望為籓鎮以潛制道子，問於太子左衛率王雅曰：「吾欲用王恭、殷仲堪，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor gradually could not reconcile himself to this and wished to choose men of contemporary renown for frontier posts to restrain Daozi in secret; he asked Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard Wang Ya, "I wish to employ Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan — what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew increasingly resentful and wished to appoint men of standing to frontier posts to check Daozi indirectly; he asked Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard Wang Ya, "I am thinking of using Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan — what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「王恭風神簡貴，志氣方嚴；

translations.literal: Ya said, 'Wang Gong's bearing is refined and lofty, his spirit upright and stern;
translations.idiomatic: Ya said, 'Wang Gong has a refined and lofty bearing, and an upright, stern spirit;

sentences.zh: 仲堪謹於細行，以文義著稱。

translations.literal: Zhongkan is careful in small conduct and is famed for literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan is meticulous in small matters and is famed for learning and letters.

sentences.zh: 然皆峻狹自是，且干略不長，若委以方面，天下無事，足以守職；

translations.literal: Yet both are harsh, narrow, and self-willed, and neither excels in practical strategy; if entrusted with a frontier command, while the realm is at peace they would suffice to hold their posts;
translations.idiomatic: Yet both are harsh, narrow-minded, and self-willed, and neither has much talent for practical affairs; if given frontier commands, they would suffice while the realm is at peace;

sentences.zh: 若其有事，必為亂階矣！」

translations.literal: but if trouble arose, they would surely become the first steps toward rebellion!'"
translations.idiomatic: but if trouble came, they would surely become the seeds of rebellion!'"

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 恭，蘊之子；

translations.literal: Gong was the son of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was the son of Wang Yun.

sentences.zh: 仲堪，融之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhongkan was the grandson of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkan was the grandson of Yin Rong.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛巳，以中書令王恭為都督青、兗、幽、并、冀五州諸軍事、兗、青二州刺史，鎮京口。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinsi, Palace Secretary Wang Gong was made Commander of all military affairs in Qing, Yan, You, Bing, and Ji, Governor of Yan and Qing, and posted at Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinsi, Palace Secretary Wang Gong was made commander of the armies of Qing, Yan, You, Bing, and Ji, Governor of Yan and Qing, and posted at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊辰，大赦。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuchen, a general amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen, the court declared a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇攻秦扶風太守齊益男於新羅堡，克之，益男走。

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang attacked the Qin Administrator of Fufeng, Qi Yinan, at Xinlou Fortress, took it, and Yinan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang attacked Former Qin Administrator of Fufeng Qi Yinan at Xinlou Fortress, took it, and Yinan fled.

sentences.zh: 秦主登攻後秦天水太守張業生於隴東，萇救之，登引去。

translations.literal: The Qin ruler Deng attacked the Later Qin Administrator of Tianshui, Zhang Yesheng, in eastern Long, and Chang went to rescue him; Deng withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin ruler Fu Deng attacked Later Qin Administrator of Tianshui Zhang Yesheng in eastern Long, and Chang marched to relieve him; Deng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，秦鎮東將軍魏揭飛自稱沖天王，帥氐、胡攻後秦安北將軍姚當成於杏城；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Qin Pacifying East General Wei Jiefei declared himself the Heaven-Striking King, led Di and Hu forces to attack Later Qin Pacifying North General Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Former Qin Pacifying East General Wei Jiefei declared himself the Heaven-Striking King and led Di and Hu forces against Later Qin Pacifying North General Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng;

sentences.zh: 鎮軍將軍雷惡地叛應之，攻鎮東將軍姚漢得於李潤。

translations.literal: Pacifying Army General Lei E'di rebelled in response and attacked Pacifying East General Yao Hande at Lirun.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying Army General Lei E'di rebelled in support and attacked Pacifying East General Yao Hande at Lirun.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇欲自擊之，群臣皆曰：「陛下不憂六十里苻登，乃憂六百里魏揭飛，何也？」

translations.literal: The Later Qin ruler Chang wished to strike them in person; all the ministers said, "Your Majesty does not worry about Fu Deng sixty li away, yet worries about Wei Jiefei six hundred li away — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang wished to strike them in person; his ministers said, "Your Majesty does not worry about Fu Deng sixty li away, yet you worry about Wei Jiefei six hundred li away — why?"

sentences.zh: 萇曰：「登非可猝滅，吾城亦非登所能猝拔。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Deng cannot be destroyed in a rush, and my cities are not ones Deng can suddenly take.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Deng cannot be destroyed overnight, and my cities are not ones he can suddenly take.

sentences.zh: 惡地智略非常，若南引揭飛，東結董成，得杏城、李潤而據之，長安東北非吾有也。」

translations.literal: E'di's wisdom and strategy are extraordinary; if he draws Jiefei southward and joins with Dong Cheng in the east, and holds Xingcheng and Lirun, the northeast of Chang'an will no longer be ours."
translations.idiomatic: E'di is extraordinarily clever and capable; if he links Jiefei to the south and Dong Cheng to the east, and holds Xingcheng and Lirun, we will lose the northeast of Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 乃潛引精兵一千六百赴之。

translations.literal: He then secretly led sixteen hundred picked troops to the scene.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly marched sixteen hundred picked troops to the scene.

sentences.zh: 揭飛、惡地有眾數萬，氐、胡赴之者首尾不絕。

translations.literal: Jiefei and E'di had tens of thousands of men, and Di and Hu who came to join them stretched out in an unbroken line.
translations.idiomatic: Jiefei and E'di had tens of thousands of men, and Di and Hu reinforcements kept arriving without end.

sentences.zh: 萇每見一軍至，輒喜。

translations.literal: Each time Chang saw another army arrive, he rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Each time another army arrived, Chang rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 群臣怪而問之，萇曰：「揭飛等扇誘同惡，種類甚繁，吾雖克其魁帥，餘黨未易猝平。

translations.literal: The ministers wondered at this and asked him; Chang said, "Jiefei and the rest have incited fellow evildoers, and their kind is very numerous; even if I defeat their chieftains, the remaining bands will not be easy to pacify at once.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were puzzled and asked why; Chang said, "Jiefei and the rest have stirred up every sort of malcontent; even if I defeat their leaders, the remaining bands will not be easy to wipe out at once.

sentences.zh: 今烏集而至，吾乘勝取之，可一舉無餘也。」

translations.literal: Now they gather like crows and come together; if I take them at the height of victory, I can destroy them in one stroke with none left."
translations.idiomatic: Now they flock here like crows; if I strike while I have the advantage, I can wipe them out in one blow."

sentences.zh: 揭飛等見後秦兵少，悉眾攻之。

translations.literal: When Jiefei and the rest saw how few Later Qin troops there were, they attacked with all their forces.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiefei and the rest saw how few Later Qin troops there were, they attacked with their full strength.

sentences.zh: 萇固壘不戰，示之以弱，潛遣其子中軍將軍崇帥騎數百出其後。

translations.literal: Chang held his camp and would not fight, showing weakness, while secretly sending his son Central Army General Chong with several hundred horsemen around behind them.
translations.idiomatic: Chang held his camp and refused battle, feigning weakness, while secretly sending his son Central Army General Yao Chong with several hundred horsemen around behind them.

sentences.zh: 揭飛兵擾亂，萇遣鎮遠將軍王超等給兵擊之，斬揭飛及其將士萬餘級。

translations.literal: Jiefei's troops fell into disorder; Chang sent Pacifying the Distance General Wang Chao and others with reinforcements to strike them, and beheaded Jiefei along with more than ten thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Jiefei's army fell into disorder; Chang sent Pacifying the Distance General Wang Chao and others with reinforcements to strike them, killing Jiefei and more than ten thousand of his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 惡地請降，萇待之如初，惡地謂人曰：「吾自謂智勇傑出上時，而每遇姚翁輒困，固其分也！」

translations.literal: E'di asked to surrender, and Chang treated him as before; E'di said to others, "I considered my wisdom and courage outstanding in my time, yet whenever I meet Old Yao I am brought to straits — such is my allotted portion!"
translations.idiomatic: E'di asked to surrender, and Chang treated him as before; E'di said to others, "I thought myself the cleverest and bravest man of my age, yet whenever I meet Old Yao I am brought to ruin — such is my fate!"

sentences.zh: 萇命姚當成於所營之地，每柵孔中輒樹一木以旌戰功。

translations.literal: Chang ordered Yao Dangcheng that in the ground where he had encamped, a tree should be planted in every gap between palisade stakes to mark battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ordered Yao Dangcheng to plant a tree in every gap between the palisade stakes in his camp to mark the battle's glory.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，問之，當成曰：「營地太小，已廣之矣。」

translations.literal: More than a year later he asked about it; Dangcheng said, "The camp ground was too small, so it has already been expanded."
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he asked about it; Dangcheng said, "The camp was too small, so we have already expanded it."

sentences.zh: 萇曰：「吾自結髮以來，與人戰，未嘗如此之快，以千餘兵破三萬之眾，營地惟小為奇，豈以大為貴哉！」

translations.literal: Chang said, "From the time I bound up my hair until now, in all my battles I have never felt such exhilaration; with little more than a thousand troops I broke thirty thousand — that the camp ground alone was small is the marvel; how could largeness be prized!"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Since I first bound up my hair, I have never fought a battle that pleased me more: with little more than a thousand men I broke thirty thousand. That the camp alone was small is the marvel — how could size be the point!"

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾視連遣使獻見於金城王乾歸，乾歸拜視連沙州牧、白蘭王。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Shilian sent envoys to offer submission and audience to King Qian'gui of Jincheng; Qian'gui invested Shilian as Governor of Shazhou and Prince of Bailand.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun Shilian sent envoys to submit to King Qifu Qian'gui of Jincheng; Qian'gui invested Shilian as Governor of Sha and Prince of Bailand.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，魏王珪會燕趙王麟於意辛山，擊賀蘭、紇突鄰、紇奚三部，破之，紇突鄰、紇奚皆降於魏。

translations.literal: On bingyin, the Wei ruler Gui met Prince Lin of Yan and Zhao at Yixin Mountain, attacked the Helan, Hetulin, and Hexi tribes, defeated them, and both Hetulin and Hexi surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Wei ruler Tuoba Gui met Prince Murong Lin of Yan and Zhao at Yixin Mountain, attacked the Helan, Hetulin, and Hexi tribes, defeated them, and both Hetulin and Hexi surrendered to Wei.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，馮詡人郭質起兵於廣鄉以應秦，移檄三輔曰：「姚萇凶虐，毒被神人。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Guo Zhi of Fengyi raised troops at Guangxiang in response to Qin and issued a proclamation to the Three Adjuncts, saying, "Yao Chang is cruel and tyrannical; his poison reaches gods and men alike.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Guo Zhi of Fengyi raised troops at Guangxiang in support of Former Qin and issued a proclamation to the Three Adjuncts: "Yao Chang is cruel and tyrannical; his poison afflicts gods and men alike.

sentences.zh: 吾屬世蒙先帝堯、舜之仁，非常伯、納言之子，即卿校、牧守之孫也。

translations.literal: Our line has for generations received the benevolence of emperors Yao and Shun; we are not merely sons of extraordinary grandees and chief speakers, but grandsons of ministers, generals, governors, and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Our families have long enjoyed the benevolence of sage emperors; we are not mere sons of high ministers and chief speakers, but grandsons of commanders, governors, and prefects.

sentences.zh: 與其含恥而存，孰若蹈道而死！」

translations.literal: Better to follow the Way and die than to live on in shame!"
translations.idiomatic: Better to die following the right path than to live on in shame!"

sentences.zh: 於是三輔壁壘皆應之；

translations.literal: Thereupon fortified strongholds throughout the Three Adjuncts all responded;
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon fortified strongholds throughout the Three Adjuncts all rose in response;

sentences.zh: 獨鄭縣人苟曜不從，聚眾數千附於後秦。

translations.literal: only Gou Yao of Zheng County did not follow, gathered several thousand men, and attached himself to Later Qin.
translations.idiomatic: only Gou Yao of Zheng County refused, gathered several thousand men, and submitted to Later Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦以質為馮翊太守；

translations.literal: Qin made Zhi Administrator of Fengyi;
translations.idiomatic: Former Qin made Guo Zhi Administrator of Fengyi;

sentences.zh: 後秦以曜為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Later Qin made Yao Inspector of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qin made Gou Yao Inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰遣子直力鞮攻賀蘭部，賀訥困急，請降於魏。

translations.literal: Liu Weichen sent his son Zhilidi to attack the Helan tribe; He Na was hard pressed and asked to surrender to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen sent his son Zhilidi to attack the Helan tribe; He Na was hard pressed and asked to surrender to Wei.

sentences.zh: 丙子，魏王珪引兵救之，直力鞮退。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Wei ruler Gui led troops to rescue him, and Zhilidi withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Wei ruler Tuoba Gui marched to relieve him, and Zhilidi withdrew.

sentences.zh: 鞮徙訥部落，處之東境。

translations.literal: Zhilidi moved Na's tribe and settled it on the eastern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilidi moved Na's tribe and settled it on Wei's eastern frontier.

sentences.zh: 八月，劉牢之擊翟釗於鄄城，釗走河北；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Liu Laozhi attacked Zhai Zhao at Juancheng; Zhao fled north of the Yellow River;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Liu Laozhi attacked Zhai Zhao at Juancheng; Zhao fled north of the river;

sentences.zh: 又敗翟遼於滑台，張願來降。

translations.literal: he also defeated Zhai Liao at Huatai, and Zhang Yuan came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: he also defeated Zhai Liao at Huatai, and Zhang Yuan came over to his side.

sentences.zh: 九月，北平人吳柱聚眾千餘，立沙門法長為天子。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wu Zhu of Beiping gathered a crowd of more than a thousand and made the monk Fachang emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wu Zhu of Beiping rallied more than a thousand men and proclaimed the monk Fachang emperor.

sentences.zh: 破北平郡，轉寇廣都，入白狼城。

translations.literal: They broke Beiping Commandery, turned to raid Guangdu, and entered White Wolf City.
translations.idiomatic: They overran Beiping commandery, turned to plunder Guangdu, and entered White Wolf City.

sentences.zh: 燕幽州牧高陽王隆方葬其夫人，郡縣守宰皆會之。

translations.literal: Yan's Inspector of You Province, Prince Murong Long of Gaoyang, was burying his wife; the governors and magistrates of the commanderies and counties had all gathered for it.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Murong Long of Gaoyang, Yan's inspector of You, was burying his wife; county and district officials had all assembled for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 眾聞柱反，請隆還城，遣大兵討之。

translations.literal: When the assembly heard Zhu had rebelled, they urged Long to return to the city and send a large force against him.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourners heard Zhu had risen in revolt, they urged Long to return to his seat and dispatch a major force against him.

sentences.zh: 隆曰：「今閭閻安業，民不思亂。

translations.literal: Long said, "The lanes and hamlets are secure in their livelihoods; the people have no thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Long said, "The common households are at peace in their work; the people have no mind for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 柱等以詐謀惑愚夫，誘脅相聚，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Zhu and his ilk use deceitful plots to beguile fools and coerce them into gathering—they can accomplish nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu and his sort deceive simple men with fraud and drag them together by force—they can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 遂留葬訖，遣廣平太守、廣都令先歸，繼遣安昌侯進將百餘騎趨白狼城。

translations.literal: He remained until the burial was finished, sent the Administrator of Guangping and the magistrate of Guangdu back first, then dispatched Marquis Jin of Anchang with more than a hundred horsemen to hurry to White Wolf City.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed until the burial was complete, sent the Guangping administrator and Guangdu magistrate back first, then dispatched Marquis Jin of Anchang with a hundred-odd horsemen to rush White Wolf City.

sentences.zh: 柱眾聞之，皆潰；

translations.literal: Zhu's followers heard of it and all scattered;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's band heard this and broke apart;

sentences.zh: 窮捕，斬之。

translations.literal: they were hunted down and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: they were hunted to the end and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 以侍中王國寶為中書令，俄兼中領軍。

translations.literal: Wang Guobao, Attendant-in-Ordinary, was made Director of the Secretariat; soon he also held the concurrent post of Central Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao, attendant-in-ordinary, was appointed director of the Secretariat and soon also took command of the central army.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以吳郡太守王珣為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Wang Xun, Administrator of Wu Commandery, was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the right.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Wang Xun, administrator of Wu commandery, was made vice director of the Masters of Writing on the right.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾視連卒，子視羆立。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun Shilian died; his son Shipi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun Shilian died, and his son Shipi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 視羆以其父祖慈仁，為四鄰所侵侮，乃督厲將士，欲建功業。

translations.literal: Shipi, because his father and grandfather had been kind and benevolent and had suffered insults from the four neighboring quarters, spurred and disciplined his officers and men, wishing to build merit and a great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Shipi, seeing how his father and grandfather's kindness had invited bullying from every neighbor, drilled his troops hard and set out to win glory on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，金城王乾歸遣使拜視羆沙州牧、白蘭王，視羆不受。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, sent envoys to invest Shipi as Governor of Shazhou and King of Bailan; Shipi refused.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Qifu Gangui, king of Jincheng, sent envoys to invest Shipi as governor of Shazhou and king of Bailan; Shipi declined.

sentences.zh: 十二月，郭質及苟曜戰於鄭東，質敗，奔洛陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Guo Zhi and Gou Yao fought east of Zheng; Zhi was defeated and fled to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Guo Zhi and Gou Yao fought east of Zheng; Zhi was beaten and fled to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 越質詰歸據平襄，叛金城王乾歸。

translations.literal: Yuezhizhi Gui held Pingxiang and rebelled against Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhizhi Gui seized Pingxiang and rebelled against Qifu Gangui, king of Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 列宗孝武皇帝中之下太元十六年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liedzong, Middle Part, Lower Scroll — the sixteenth year of Taixuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of the Liedzong, middle part, lower scroll — the sixteenth year of Taixuan (

sentences.zh: 辛卯，公元三九一年）

translations.literal: xinj mao — the year 391 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinj mao — 391 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，燕置行台於薊，加長樂公盛錄行台文書事。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Yan established a Mobile Secretariat at Ji and added Prince Sheng of Changle as recorder of Mobile Secretariat documents.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Yan set up a mobile secretariat at Ji and made Prince Sheng of Changle recorder of its documents.

sentences.zh: 金城王乾歸擊越質詰歸，詰歸降，乾歸以宗女妻之。

translations.literal: Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, attacked Yuezhizhi Gui; Gui submitted, and Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Qifu Gangui attacked Yuezhizhi Gui; Gui surrendered, and Gangui gave him a clanswoman in marriage.

sentences.zh: 賀染干謀殺其兄訥，訥知之，舉兵相攻。

translations.literal: He Rangan plotted to kill his elder brother Ne; Ne learned of it and raised troops to fight him.
translations.idiomatic: He Rangan plotted to kill his elder brother Ne; Ne found out and raised troops to attack him.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪告於燕，請為鄉導以討之。

translations.literal: King Tuoba Gui of Wei informed Yan and asked to serve as guide in attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: King Tuoba Gui of Wei notified Yan and offered to guide an expedition against them.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲戌，燕主垂遣趙王麟將兵擊訥，鎮北將軍蘭汗帥龍城之兵擊染干。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiaxu, Yan ruler Murong Chui sent Prince Murong Lin of Zhao with troops against Ne, and Pacifying-North General Lan Han led the Longcheng army against Rangan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiaxu, Murong Chui sent Prince Murong Lin of Zhao against Ne while Pacifying-North General Lan Han led the Longcheng army against Rangan.

sentences.zh: 三月，秦主登自雍攻後秦安東將軍金榮於范氏堡，克之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Fu Deng of Qin advanced from Yong to attack Later Qin's Pacifying-East General Jin Rong at the Fan clan fortress and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Fu Deng of Former Qin marched from Yong against Later Qin's pacifying-east general Jin Rong at the Fan clan fortress and took it.

sentences.zh: 遂渡渭水，攻京兆太守韋范於段氏堡，不克，進據曲牢。

translations.literal: He then crossed the Wei River and attacked Wei Fan, Administrator of Jingzhao, at the Duan clan fortress but failed to take it, and advanced to hold Qu'lao.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Wei River and assaulted Wei Fan, Jingzhao administrator, at the Duan clan fortress; failing there, he pressed on to occupy Qu'lao.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，燕蘭汗破賀染干於牛都。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Lan Han of Yan defeated He Rangan at Niudu.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Lan Han of Yan routed He Rangan at Niudu.

sentences.zh: 苟曜有眾一萬，密召秦主登，許為內應。

translations.literal: Gou Yao had ten thousand men and secretly summoned Fu Deng of Qin, promising to serve as an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yao commanded ten thousand men and secretly summoned Fu Deng, offering to act as an inside ally.

sentences.zh: 登自曲牢向繁川，軍於馬頭原。

translations.literal: Deng marched from Qu'lao toward Fanchuan and encamped at Matou Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Deng moved from Qu'lao toward Fanchuan and encamped at Horse Head Plain.

sentences.zh: 五月，後秦主萇引兵逆戰，登擊破之，斬其右將軍吳忠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Later Qin ruler Yao Chang led troops to meet him in battle; Deng struck and defeated him and beheaded his Right General Wu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Yao Chang of Later Qin marched out to give battle; Deng broke his line and beheaded Right General Wu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 萇收眾復戰，姚碩德曰：「陛下慎於輕戰，每欲以計取之，今戰失利而更前逼賊，何也？」

translations.literal: Chang rallied his troops and fought again; Yao Shuode said, "Your Majesty is wary of fighting lightly and always wishes to take the enemy by stratagem—now that the battle has gone badly, why advance again and press the foe?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang regrouped and fought again; Yao Shuode said, "Your Majesty avoids rash battle and prefers to win by stratagem—why, after a defeat, press forward on the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 萇曰：「登用兵遲緩，不識虛實。

translations.literal: Chang said, "Deng is slow in the use of troops and does not discern truth from falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Deng is slow on the march and cannot read strength from bluff.

sentences.zh: 今輕兵直進，遙據吾東，此必苟曜豎子與之有謀也。

translations.literal: That he advances lightly and straight on, holding our east from afar—this must be because that boy Gou Yao has a plot with him.
translations.idiomatic: His light force has pushed straight ahead and holds our eastern flank from afar—that can only mean the wretch Gou Yao is in league with him.

sentences.zh: 緩之則其謀得成，故及其交之未合，急擊之，以敗散其事耳。」

translations.literal: If we delay, their plot will succeed; therefore, before their alliance is joined, we must strike hard to break and scatter their scheme."
translations.idiomatic: Delay would let their plot ripen; I mean to strike before their hands meet and smash the whole design."

sentences.zh: 遂進戰，大破之。

translations.literal: He then pressed the battle and routed Deng's army.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the attack and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 登退屯於郿。

translations.literal: Deng withdrew and encamped at Mei.
translations.idiomatic: Deng pulled back and encamped at Mei.

sentences.zh: 秦兗州刺史強金槌據新平，降後秦，以其子逵為質。

translations.literal: Qiang Jinchui, Inspector of Yan Province in Qin, held Xinping, submitted to Later Qin, and sent his son Kui as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Jinchui, Former Qin's inspector of Yan, held Xinping, submitted to Later Qin, and sent his son Kui as hostage.

sentences.zh: 後秦主萇將數百騎入金槌營。

translations.literal: Later Qin ruler Yao Chang led several hundred horsemen into Jinchui's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang of Later Qin rode into Jinchui's camp with only a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 群下諫之，萇曰：「金槌既去苻登，又欲圖我，將安所歸乎？

translations.literal: His officers warned against it; Chang said, "Jinchui has already turned from Fu Deng and now would scheme against me—where else could he go?
translations.idiomatic: His officers protested; Chang said, "Jinchui has already broken with Fu Deng—if he plots against me too, where can he turn?

sentences.zh: 且彼初來款附，宜推心以結之，奈何復以不信疑之乎？」

translations.literal: Besides, he has just come in sincere submission—we ought to win him with an open heart. Why doubt him again with distrust?"
translations.idiomatic: And he has only just submitted in good faith—we should meet him with open trust. Why greet him with suspicion?"

sentences.zh: 既而群氐欲取萇，金槌不從。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the mass of Di wished to seize Chang, but Jinchui would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Di in his ranks wanted to seize Chang, but Jinchui refused.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲辰，燕趙王麟破賀訥於赤城，禽之，降其部落數萬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Murong Lin, Prince of Zhao in Yan, defeated He Ne at Red City, captured him, and received the submission of his tribes numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Prince Murong Lin of Zhao defeated He Ne at Red City, captured him, and brought tens of thousands of his tribesmen to submission.

sentences.zh: 燕主垂命麟歸訥部落，徙染干於中山。

translations.literal: Murong Chui ordered Lin to restore Ne to his tribe and moved Rangan to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui ordered Lin to restore Ne to his tribe and resettled Rangan at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 麟歸，言於垂曰：「臣觀拓跋珪舉動，終為國患，不若攝之還朝，使其弟監國事。」

translations.literal: When Lin returned, he told Chui, "Your servant observes Tuoba Gui's conduct—he will become a calamity to the state. Better to summon him back to court and have his younger brother oversee affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: On his return Lin told Chui, "I have watched Tuoba Gui's every move—he will be a plague on the realm. Better summon him to court and leave his younger brother to govern Wei."

sentences.zh: 垂不從。

translations.literal: Chui did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Chui would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 西燕主永寇河南，太守楊佺期擊破之。

translations.literal: Murong Yong, lord of Western Yan, raided Henan; Administrator Yang Quanqi defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong of Western Yan raided Henan; Administrator Yang Quanqi drove him off.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬申，燕主垂如范陽。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on renshen, Murong Chui went to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renshen, Murong Chui traveled to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪遣其弟觚獻見於燕，燕主垂衰老，子弟用事，留觚以求良馬。

translations.literal: King Tuoba Gui of Wei sent his younger brother Gu on a mission of tribute to Yan. Murong Chui was aged, his younger kinsmen held power, and they detained Gu to demand fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: King Tuoba Gui of Wei sent his brother Gu to pay court to Yan. Chui was old, his younger kinsmen ran affairs, and they held Gu hostage to extort fine horses.

sentences.zh: 魏王珪弗與，遂與燕絕，使長史張袞求好於西燕。

translations.literal: Tuoba Gui would not give them and broke with Yan; he sent chief clerk Zhang Gun to seek friendship with Western Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Gui refused and broke with Yan, sending chief clerk Zhang Gun to seek an alliance with Western Yan.

sentences.zh: 觚逃歸，燕太子寶追獲之，垂待之如初。

translations.literal: Gu escaped home; Crown Prince Bao pursued and recaptured him, but Chui treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Gu escaped home; Crown Prince Bao ran him down and recaptured him, yet Chui treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 秦主登攻新平，後秦主萇救之，登引去。

translations.literal: Fu Deng of Qin attacked Xinping; Yao Chang of Later Qin came to its relief, and Deng withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng attacked Xinping; Yao Chang marched to relieve it, and Deng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 秦驃騎將軍沒弈干以其二子為質於金城王乾歸，請共擊鮮卑大兜。

translations.literal: Mo Yigan, Qin's General of Rapid Cavalry, sent his two sons as hostages to Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng, and asked to join in attacking the Xianbei chief Da'er.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Yigan, Former Qin's general of rapid cavalry, sent his two sons as hostages to Qifu Gangui and asked to join him against the Xianbei chief Da'er.

sentences.zh: 乾歸與沒弈干攻大兜於鳴蟬堡，克之。

translations.literal: Gangui and Mo Yigan attacked Da'er at Mingchan Fortress and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Gangui and Mo Yigan stormed Da'er at Mingchan Fortress and took it.

sentences.zh: 兜微服走，乾歸收其部眾而還，歸沒弈干二子。

translations.literal: Da'er fled in disguised dress; Gangui gathered his followers and returned, restoring Mo Yigan's two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Da'er slipped away in disguise; Gangui gathered his followers, returned, and restored Mo Yigan's two sons.

sentences.zh: 沒弈干尋叛，東合劉衛辰。

translations.literal: Mo Yigan soon rebelled and joined Liu Weichen in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Yigan soon rebelled and joined Liu Weichen in the east.

sentences.zh: 八月，乾歸帥騎一萬討沒弈干，沒弈干奔他樓城，乾歸射之，中目。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Gangui led ten thousand horsemen to chastise Mo Yigan; Mo Yigan fled to Talou City, and Gangui shot him in the eye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Gangui led ten thousand horsemen against Mo Yigan; Mo Yigan fled to Talou City, and Gangui's arrow found his eye.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸未，以尚書右僕射王珣為左僕射，太子詹事謝琰為右僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guiwei, Wang Xun, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the right, was made Vice Director on the left, and Xie Yan, Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Vice Director on the right.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guiwei, Wang Xun was moved from vice director on the right to vice director on the left, and Xie Yan, grand tutor of the heir apparent, became vice director on the right.

sentences.zh: 太學博士范弘之訟殷浩宜加贈謚，因敘桓溫不臣之跡。

translations.literal: Imperial Academy Erudite Fan Hongzhi petitioned that Yin Hao should receive a posthumous enfeoffment and title, and in doing so recounted Huan Wen's disloyal acts.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Academy erudite Fan Hongzhi petitioned that Yin Hao deserved a posthumous title and, in making his case, laid out Huan Wen's treasonous conduct.

sentences.zh: 是時桓氏猶盛，王珣，溫之故吏也，以為溫廢昏立明，有忠貞之節；

translations.literal: At that time the Huan clan was still powerful; Wang Xun had been an old officer of Wen's and held that Wen had deposed the benighted and established the enlightened—a mark of loyal integrity;
translations.idiomatic: The Huan clan was still powerful; Wang Xun, a former officer of Wen's, argued that Wen had deposed a benighted ruler and enthroned a worthy one—proof of loyal integrity;

sentences.zh: 黜弘之為餘杭令。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was demoted to magistrate of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was demoted to magistrate of Yuhang.

sentences.zh: 弘之，汪之孫也。

translations.literal: Hongzhi was the grandson of Fan Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi was Fan Wang's grandson.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬辰，燕主垂還中山。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renchen, Murong Chui returned to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renchen, Murong Chui returned to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 初，柔然部人世服於代，其大人郁久閭地粟袁卒，部落分為二：長子匹候跋繼父居東邊，次子縕紇提別居西邊。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Rouran people had long served Dai; their chieftain Yujulü Duisugan died, and the tribe split in two—the eldest son Pihouba succeeded his father on the east, the second son Wenheti settled separately on the west.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, the Rouran had served Dai; when their chieftain Yujulü Duisugan died the tribe split—eldest son Pihouba kept the east, second son Wenheti settled apart in the west.

sentences.zh: 秦王堅滅代，柔然附於劉衛辰。

translations.literal: When King Fu Jian of Qin destroyed Dai, the Rouran attached themselves to Liu Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: When King Fu Jian of Former Qin destroyed Dai, the Rouran attached themselves to Liu Weichen.

sentences.zh: 及魏王珪即位，攻擊高車等，諸部率皆服從，獨柔然不事魏。

translations.literal: When King Tuoba Gui of Wei came to the throne, he attacked the Gaoche and other peoples; the various tribes mostly submitted, but Rouran alone would not serve Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuoba Gui came to the Wei throne and attacked the Gaoche and other tribes, nearly all submitted—only the Rouran refused to serve Wei.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，珪引兵擊之，柔然舉部遁走，珪追奔六百里。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Gui led troops against them; Rouran rose as a whole and fled, and Gui pursued them six hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Gui marched against them; the whole Rouran nation fled, and Gui chased them six hundred li.

sentences.zh: 諸將因張袞言於珪曰：「賊遠糧盡，不如早還。」

translations.literal: The generals, through Zhang Gun, said to Gui, "The enemy is far off and our grain is spent—we had better return soon."
translations.idiomatic: Through Zhang Gun the generals urged Gui, "The foe is far and our grain is gone—we should turn back."

sentences.zh: 珪問諸將：「若殺副馬，為三日食，足乎？」

translations.literal: Gui asked the generals, "If we slaughter the spare horses for three days' rations, will that suffice?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui asked his commanders, "If we slaughter the remounts for three days' food, will that be enough?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「足。」

translations.literal: All said, "It will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "It will."

sentences.zh: 乃復倍道追之，及於大磧南床山下，大破之，虜其半部，匹候跋及別部帥屋擊各收餘眾遁走。

translations.literal: They doubled their pace in pursuit, caught them at South Bed Mountain on the great desert, and routed them heavily, taking half the tribe captive; Pihouba and the separate-branch leader Wuji each gathered what remained and fled.
translations.idiomatic: They doubled their pace, caught the Rouran at South Bed Mountain on the great desert, and broke them badly, taking half the tribe; Pihouba and the branch chief Wuji each gathered what was left and fled.

sentences.zh: 珪遣長孫嵩、長孫肥追之。

translations.literal: Gui sent Changsun Song and Changsun Fei in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sent Changsun Song and Changsun Fei in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 珪謂將佐曰：「卿曹知吾前問三日意乎？」

translations.literal: Gui said to his officers, "Do you know what I meant by asking about three days' food before?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui asked his officers, "Do you understand why I asked about three days' rations?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「不知也。」

translations.literal: They said, "We do not."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "We do not."

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「柔然驅畜產奔走數日，至水必留；

translations.literal: Gui said, "Rouran drives their herds in flight for days on end—when they reach water they must halt;
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "The Rouran drive their herds hard for days—when they reach water they must stop;

sentences.zh: 我以輕騎追之，計期道裡，不過三日及之矣。」

translations.literal: I meant to overtake them with light horse in no more than three days by the road we would travel."
translations.idiomatic: I reckoned our light cavalry would overtake them within three days on the road."

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「非所及也！」

translations.literal: All said, "Beyond what we could have foreseen!"
translations.idiomatic: All said, "We never saw that coming!"

sentences.zh: 嵩追斬屋擊於平望川。

translations.literal: Song pursued and killed Wuji at Pingwang Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Song ran down Wuji and killed him at Pingwang Stream.

sentences.zh: 肥追匹候跋至涿邪山，匹候跋舉從降，獲縕紇提之子曷多汗、兄子社侖、斛律等宗黨數百人。

translations.literal: Fei pursued Pihouba to Zhuo'e Mountain; Pihouba brought his followers and submitted, and they captured Wenheti's son Yiduo Han, his nephew Shelun, Helü, and several hundred clan members.
translations.idiomatic: Fei chased Pihouba to Zhuo'e Mountain; Pihouba surrendered with his followers, and they took Wenheti's son Yiduo Han, nephew Shelun, Helü, and several hundred kinsmen.

sentences.zh: 縕紇提將奔劉衛辰，珪追及之，縕紇提亦降，珪悉徙其部眾於雲中。

translations.literal: Wenheti was about to flee to Liu Weichen; Gui overtook him, Wenheti too submitted, and Gui moved all their people to Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenheti was heading for Liu Weichen; Gui overtook him, Wenheti surrendered too, and Gui moved all their people to Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 翟遼卒，子釗代立，改元定鼎。

translations.literal: Zhai Liao died; his son Zhao succeeded him and changed the era name to Dingding.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao died; his son Zhao succeeded him and adopted the era name Dingding.

sentences.zh: 攻燕鄴城，燕遼西王農擊卻之。

translations.literal: He attacked Ye, the capital fort of Yan; Prince Murong Nong of Liaoxi drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yan's city of Ye; Prince Murong Nong of Liaoxi beat him back.

sentences.zh: 三河王光遣兵乘虛伐金城王乾歸，乾歸聞之，引兵還，光兵亦退。

translations.literal: Wang Guang, Prince of Sanhe, sent troops to exploit a gap and strike Qifu Gangui, King of Jincheng; Gangui heard of it, led his army back, and Guang's troops also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guang, prince of Sanhe, sent troops to strike Qifu Gangui while he was away; Gangui turned back on hearing of it, and Guang's army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉衛辰遣子直力鞮帥眾八九萬攻魏南部。

translations.literal: Liu Weichen sent his son Zhili Diji at the head of eighty or ninety thousand men to attack Wei's southern lands.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weichen sent his son Zhili Diji with eighty or ninety thousand men against Wei's south.

sentences.zh: 十一月，已卯，魏王珪引兵五六千人拒之，壬午，大破直力鞮於鐵岐山南，直力鞮單騎走。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jimao, King Tuoba Gui of Wei led five or six thousand men to oppose him; on renwu he routed Zhili Diji south of Iron Qi Mountain, and Zhili Diji fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jimao, Tuoba Gui met him with five or six thousand men; on renwu he crushed Zhili Diji south of Iron Qi Mountain, and Zhili Diji fled alone.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追之，戊子，自五原金津南濟河，逕入衛辰國，衛辰部落駭亂。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit, on wuzi he crossed the river south from Wuyuan's Golden Ford and went straight into Weichen's territory; Weichen's tribes were thrown into panic.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory, on wuzi he crossed the river south from Wuyuan's Golden Ford and plunged straight into Weichen's lands; Weichen's tribes panicked.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，珪直抵其所居悅跋城，衛辰父子出走。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Gui went straight to Yueba City where they lived; Weichen and his sons fled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Gui marched straight to Yueba City, Weichen's seat; Weichen and his sons fled.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，分遣諸將輕騎追之。

translations.literal: On renchen, he sent out his generals in light cavalry in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, he sent his generals in light cavalry in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 將軍伊謂禽直力珪於木根山，衛辰為其部下所殺。

translations.literal: General Yiyi captured Zhili Diji at Mugen Mountain; Weichen was killed by his own men.
translations.idiomatic: General Yiyi captured Zhili Diji at Mugen Mountain; Weichen was killed by his own followers.

sentences.zh: 十二月，珪軍於鹽池，誅衛辰宗黨五千餘人，皆投屍於河。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Gui encamped at Salt Pool, executed more than five thousand of Weichen's clan and partisans, and cast their bodies into the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Gui encamped at Salt Pool, executed more than five thousand of Weichen's clan and partisans, and threw their bodies into the river.

sentences.zh: 自河以南諸部悉降，獲馬三十餘萬匹，牛羊四百餘萬頭，國用由是遂饒。

translations.literal: All the tribes south of the river submitted; they took more than three hundred thousand horses and more than four million head of cattle and sheep, and from this the state's resources became abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Every tribe south of the river submitted; they took more than three hundred thousand horses and over four million head of cattle and sheep, and the realm's stores grew rich.

sentences.zh: 衛辰少子勃勃亡奔薛幹部，珪使人求之，薛幹部帥太悉伏出勃勃以示使者曰：「勃勃國破家亡，以窮歸我，我寧與之俱亡，何忍執以與魏！」

translations.literal: Weichen's youngest son Bobo fled to the Xuegan tribe; Gui sent men to demand him; Xuegan chieftain Taixifu brought Bobo out to show the envoy and said, "Bobo's state is broken and his house destroyed—he came to me in extremity. I would rather perish with him than hand him over to Wei!"
translations.idiomatic: Weichen's youngest son Bobo fled to the Xuegan tribe; Gui sent men to demand him. Xuegan chief Taixifu produced Bobo before the envoy and said, "His state is broken and his house destroyed—he came to me in desperation. I would rather die with him than hand him to Wei!"

sentences.zh: 乃送勃勃於沒弈干，沒弈干以女妻之。

translations.literal: He then sent Bobo to Mo Yigan, and Mo Yigan gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Bobo to Mo Yigan, who gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 戊申，燕主垂如魯口。

translations.literal: On wushen, Murong Chui went to Lukou.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Murong Chui went to Lukou.

sentences.zh: 秦主登攻安定，後秦主萇如陰密以拒之，謂太子興曰：「苟曜聞吾北行，必來見汝，汝執誅之。」

translations.literal: Fu Deng of Qin attacked Anding; Yao Chang of Later Qin went to Yinmi to oppose him and told Crown Prince Yao Xing, "When Gou Yao hears I am marching north, he will surely come to see you—seize and execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Deng attacked Anding; Yao Chang went to Yinmi to block him and told Crown Prince Yao Xing, "When Gou Yao hears I have marched north, he will come to see you—seize him and kill him."

sentences.zh: 曜果見興於長安，興使尹緯讓而誅之。

translations.literal: Gou Yao did come to see Xing at Chang'an; Xing had Yin Wei reprove him and then executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Yao did come to Xing at Chang'an; Xing had Yin Wei rebuke him and then executed him.

sentences.zh: 萇敗登於安定城東，登退據路承堡。

translations.literal: Chang defeated Deng east of Anding city; Deng withdrew to hold Lucheng Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Chang defeated Deng east of Anding; Deng fell back to Lucheng Fort.

sentences.zh: 萇置酒高會，諸將皆曰：「若值魏武王，不令此賊至今，陛下將牢太過耳。」

translations.literal: Chang held a grand banquet; the generals all said, "Had we met Prince Wu of Wei, this bandit would not have survived till today—Your Majesty is far too lenient."
translations.idiomatic: Chang held a triumph feast; the generals said, "Had Prince Wu of Wei—your brother Yao Xiang—still lived, this bandit would not be breathing; Your Majesty keeps your cage too loose."

sentences.zh: 萇笑曰：「吾不如亡兄有四：身長八尺五寸、臂垂過膝，人望而畏之，一也；

translations.literal: Chang smiled and said, "I fall short of my late brother in four things: eight feet five in height, arms hanging past the knees—men saw him and feared him; that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: Chang laughed and said, "I am no match for my dead brother in four ways: eight feet five, arms past the knees—men looked on him with dread; that is the first;

sentences.zh: 將十萬之眾，與天下爭衡，望麾而進，前無橫隈，二也；

translations.literal: commanding a host of a hundred thousand, contending with the empire—at a wave of his standard they advanced, with no obstacle before them; that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: leading a hundred thousand men against the realm, they advanced at a wave of his banner with no barrier before them; that is the second;

sentences.zh: 溫古知今，講論道藝，收羅英雋，三也；

translations.literal: warming antiquity and knowing the present, discoursing on the Way and the arts, gathering the lofty and gifted; that is the third;
translations.idiomatic: mastering antiquity and the present, discoursing on the Way and the arts, gathering the finest minds; that is the third;

sentences.zh: 董帥兄眾，上下鹹悅，人盡死力，四也。

translations.literal: leading the masses as elder brother, above and below all pleased, every man giving his utmost; that is the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: leading the host like an elder brother, high and low alike content, every man giving his all; that is the fourth.

sentences.zh: 所以得建立功業、驅策群賢者，正望算略中有片長耳。」

translations.literal: The reason I have been able to establish achievements and drive the host of worthies is precisely that I hoped to have some small strength in planning and strategy."
translations.idiomatic: The reason I have been able to build this enterprise and lead so many able men is that I hoped to have at least a little talent for strategy."

sentences.zh: 群臣咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: All the ministers together shouted Ten thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: The whole court cried Long live Your Majesty!
